title: COLI-Net: Deep learning-assisted fully automated COVID-19 lung and infection pneumonia lesion detection and segmentation from chest computed tomography images
main_contribution: Development of COLI-Net, a deep learning-based automated framework for whole lung and COVID-19 pneumonia lesion segmentation from chest CT, using transfer learning from a large multicentric lung dataset to lesion segmentation, and evaluated on multiple external datasets.

title: Deep Learning from Dual-Energy Information for Whole-Heart Segmentation in Dual-Energy and Single-Energy Non-Contrast-Enhanced Cardiac CT
organs: ["Left ventricular myocardium", "Left ventricular cavity", "Right ventricle", "Left atrium", "Right atrium", "Ascending aorta", "Pulmonary artery trunk"]
main_contribution: Developed a deep learning method for whole-heart segmentation in non-contrast-enhanced CT (NCCT) by training on virtual non-contrast (VNC) images derived from dual-energy CT, thereby avoiding the need for manual annotation in NCCT.

title: Research-based clinical deployment of artificial intelligence algorithm for prostate MRI
main_contribution: Demonstrates the feasibility of real-time deployment of a deep learning-based prostate and lesion segmentation pipeline directly into a clinical PACS environment using MONAI Deploy Express, with prospective evaluation in two phases (diagnostic imaging and biopsy planning).

title: Fully automated AI-based splenic segmentation for predicting survival and estimating the risk of hepatic decompensation in TACE patients with HCC
main_contribution: Developed a deep learning algorithm for fully automated splenic volume assessment from CT scans and validated its prognostic value for survival and hepatic decompensation in HCC patients undergoing TACE.

title: External validation, radiological evaluation, and development of deep learning automatic lung segmentation in contrast-enhanced chest CT
main_contribution: Development of a 3D nnU-Net-based lung segmentation model specifically for contrast-enhanced CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA), with clinical radiological evaluation and external validation in two diverse cohorts (pulmonary hypertension and interstitial lung disease).

title: Effect of Dataset Size and Medical Image Modality on Convolutional Neural Network Model Performance for Automated Segmentation: A CT and MR Renal Tumor Imaging Study
main_contribution: The paper proposes an exponential-plateau model to estimate the training dataset size required to reach maximum segmentation performance. It applies this model to CT and MR renal tumor and kidney segmentation using nnU-Net, and also on the KiTS21 dataset to compare 2D and 3D architectures.

title: Automatic delineation of organs at risk in non-small cell lung cancer radiotherapy based on deep learning networks
main_contribution: Proposes an end-to-end FC_DenseNet model for automatic segmentation of OARs (lungs, cord, heart) in NSCLC CT images, demonstrating improved performance over U-Net and significant time savings compared to manual segmentation.

title: Comprehensive 3D Analysis of the Renal System and Stones: Segmenting and Registering Non-Contrast and Contrast Computed Tomography Images
main_contribution: Develops an ensemble framework that combines deep learning segmentation and rigid registration to reconstruct a comprehensive 3D model of the kidney, including stones, arteries, cortex, medulla, collecting system, and parenchyma, from three-phase CT scans (non-contrast, corticomedullary, and excretory).

title: Automatic Cardiac Structure Contouring for Small Datasets with Cascaded Deep Learning Models
main_contribution: Development of a two-stage cascaded deep learning pipeline for automatic cardiac structure contouring (whole heart, ventricles, atria) on low-dose non-contrast planning CT scans using a small dataset (50 scans). The pipeline uses a slice classifier (InceptionResNetV2) to identify slices containing the heart, followed by three UNet3+ networks (axial, coronal, sagittal) that segment structures and are combined via multiplication. Achieves good Dice scores for whole heart and ventricles, but lower for atria.

title: Development of deep learning-based novel auto-segmentation for the prostatic urethra on planning CT images for prostate cancer radiotherapy
main_contribution: Developed a deep learning-based method to estimate the prostatic urethra position from bladder and prostate contours (without CT images) for patients undergoing external beam radiation therapy (EBRT), achieving a mean centerline distance of ~2.05 mm with a large test set (86 cases).

title: Open-source, fully-automated hybrid cardiac substructure segmentation: development and optimisation
main_contribution: Development of a fully-automated, open-source hybrid segmentation method that combines deep learning (nnU-Net) for whole heart segmentation, a novel whole-heart-guided multi-atlas mapping for chambers and great vessels, and geometric modelling for small structures (valves, coronary arteries, conduction nodes). The method segments 18 cardiac substructures on CT scans and is designed to handle variable imaging conditions.

title: Automatic Liver Segmentation from Multiphase CT Using Modified SegNet and ASPP Module
main_contribution: Developed a modified SegNet architecture incorporating an ASPP module and leaky ReLU layers for automatic liver segmentation from multiphase CT volumes, achieving high Dice coefficients (>96% on portal venous phase and CHAOS dataset) with reduced learnable parameters compared to standard SegNet.

title: Deep learning-based whole-heart segmentation in 4D contrast-enhanced cardiac CT
main_contribution: Developed and evaluated a deep learning-based method for automatic whole-heart segmentation (LV cavity, LV myocardium, RV, LA, RA) in 4D contrast-enhanced cardiac CT, using a large clinical dataset of TAVI patients. The method produces clinically useful segmentations across the cardiac cycle, enabling potential assessment of cardiac function.

title: Validation of a deep-learning segmentation model for adult and pediatric head and neck radiotherapy in different patient positions
main_contribution: Validation of a commercial deep-learning segmentation model for 16 head and neck OARs across eight patient orientations, using geometric, qualitative, and dose-volume analyses, and implementation for clinical use in HFS straight and hyperextended positions.

title: Autodelineation methods in a simulated fully automated proton therapy workflow for esophageal cancer
main_contribution: Evaluated different autodelineation methods (deep learning segmentation, rigid and deformable image registration) for organs-at-risk and clinical target volume in a simulated proton online adaptive radiotherapy workflow for esophageal cancer, and assessed the feasibility of fully automated planning using these contours.

title: Measurement of Glomerular Filtration Rate using Quantitative SPECT/CT and Deep-learning-based Kidney Segmentation
main_contribution: Developed a fully automated deep learning method for 3D kidney parenchyma segmentation in CT, enabling fast and accurate GFR quantification from SPECT/CT.

title: Medical imaging deep learning with differential privacy
main_contribution: The paper presents deepee, an open-source PyTorch framework for differentially private deep learning, implementing a parallelized DP-SGD algorithm that is compatible with any neural network architecture. It demonstrates the framework on medical image classification (chest radiographs) and semantic segmentation (liver CT), showing that strong privacy guarantees can be achieved with minimal performance loss in segmentation.

title: Deep 3D attention CLSTM U-Net based automated liver segmentation and volumetry for the liver transplantation in abdominal CT volumes
main_contribution: Proposes DALU-Net, a deep 3D CNN combining attention mechanism, deep supervision, and convolutional LSTM for automated liver segmentation and volumetry from abdominal CT, with evaluation on left, right, caudate lobes and whole liver.

title: Evaluation of a hybrid pipeline for automated segmentation of solid lesions based on mathematical algorithms and deep learning
main_contribution: Proposes a hybrid segmentation pipeline combining a variational (mathematical) model with a CNN, using registration to automate initial segmentation and unlabeled data to augment training. Evaluated on aortic CTs, brain tumours (BraTS), and abdominal organs, showing improved accuracy over a standard deep learning baseline.

title: Deep supervision and atrous inception-based U-Net combining CRF for automatic liver segmentation from CT
main_contribution: Proposes DA-UNet, a 3D U-Net variant with residual blocks, an atrous inception module, deep supervision, and CRF post-processing for accurate liver segmentation from CT scans.

title: Localization of spleen and kidney organs from CT scans based on classification of slices in rotational views
main_contribution: Proposes a novel method for kidney and spleen localization and segmentation in CT scans using three CNNs that classify slices in X, Y, and Z projections, followed by ROI detection and fuzzy K-means clustering for final contour extraction.

title: Graph matching and deep neural networks based whole heart and great vessel segmentation in congenital heart disease
main_contribution: Proposes a hybrid framework combining deep learning (U-Nets) for segmenting heart chambers and myocardium with graph matching for classifying great vessels, specifically designed for congenital heart disease (CHD) CT images. Achieves a 12% average Dice improvement over the state-of-the-art method for normal anatomy.

title: Estimation of right lobe graft weight for living donor liver transplantation using deep learning-based fully automatic computed tomographic volumetry
main_contribution: Developed a fully automatic deep learning pipeline for right lobe graft weight estimation in living donor liver transplantation, consisting of liver segmentation, left/right lobe classification, and volume-to-weight conversion.

title: AI-based segmentation of renal enhanced CT images for quantitative evaluate of chronic kidney disease
main_contribution: Developed a 3D nnU-Net model for automatic segmentation of renal parenchyma and cortex from enhanced CT images, and used it to quantitatively evaluate CKD by correlating volumes and CT values with renal function. Proposed gender-specific threshold values for CKD diagnosis.

title: Efficient knowledge distillation for liver CT segmentation using growing assistant network
main_contribution: Proposes a knowledge distillation (KD) framework with a growing teacher assistant network (GTAN) to compress a 3D U-net for liver CT segmentation, achieving teacher-level performance with only 8% parameters and further improving a 2% parameter student model.

title: Clinical Assessment of Deep Learning-Based Uncertainty Maps in Lung Cancer Segmentation
main_contribution: Develops a probabilistic auto-contouring system using a 3D U-Net with Monte Carlo dropout to generate probability and uncertainty maps for lung cancer CT segmentation, and clinically validates these maps with a radiation oncologist.

title: 3D Densely Connected Convolution Neural Networks for Pulmonary Parenchyma Segmentation from CT Images
main_contribution: Proposes a 3D densely connected convolutional neural network for automatic pulmonary parenchyma segmentation from CT images, achieving higher Dice coefficient (0.972) than 3D-Unet (0.923) with only half the parameters (9.1M vs 19.0M).

title: Segmentation and Reconstruction of Abdominal Multi-tissues Based on Multiple Algorithms and Networks
architecture: V-net (for liver and lesions); threshold segmentation (skin/bones); FCM clustering (blood vessels)
main_contribution: The paper presents an integrated system for automatic segmentation and 3D reconstruction of multiple abdominal tissues (skin, bones, intrahepatic blood vessels, liver, and lesions) from CT scans, combining traditional methods (threshold segmentation, fuzzy C-means) with a deep learning approach (V-net). The system also supports human-computer interaction for correction and provides 3D surface reconstruction and volume measurement.

title: COLI-NET: Fully Automated COVID-19 Lung and Infection Pneumonia Lesion Detection and Segmentation from Chest CT Images
main_contribution: Development of COLI-Net, a deep learning-based automated segmentation framework for whole lungs and COVID-19 pneumonia lesions from chest CT, using transfer learning from lung to lesion segmentation and evaluated on multi-center external datasets.

title: Deep learning-based detection of murine congenital heart defects from µCT scans
main_contribution: Development and validation of a fully automated deep learning pipeline for heart segmentation and congenital heart defect (CHD) diagnosis from mouse µCT scans, packaged as a user-friendly Napari plugin.

title: AI-enabled CT-guided end-to-end quantification of total cardiac activity in 18FDG cardiac PET/CT for detection of cardiac sarcoidosis
main_contribution: Development of a fully automated pipeline for quantifying 18FDG PET activity in cardiac sarcoidosis using deep learning segmentation of CT attenuation maps, enabling rapid (~16 seconds) and reproducible measurement of cardiac inflammation without manual annotation.

title: Applications of Synthetic Data Integration for Deep Learning for Volumetric Analysis and Segmentation in Thoracic CT Imaging
main_contribution: Development of a framework for generating synthetic objects in DICOM CT images, with Monte Carlo volume estimation, and application of UNet models for segmentation of thoracic organs and pathologies (hemothorax, pneumothorax).

title: AHCNet: An Application of Attention Mechanism and Hybrid Connection for Liver Tumor Segmentation in CT Volumes
architecture: AHCNet (3D FCN with attention hybrid connection blocks)
main_contribution: Proposes AHCNet, a cascaded 3D FCN architecture combining soft and hard attention mechanisms with hybrid (long and short) skip connections for liver and tumor segmentation in CT volumes.

title: An Augmentation Strategy for Medical Image Processing Based on Statistical Shape Model and 3D Thin Plate Spline for Deep Learning
main_contribution: Proposes a novel data augmentation strategy that combines statistical shape modeling (SSM) and 3D thin plate spline (3D-TPS) to generate realistic simulated medical images for training deep learning segmentation networks, addressing the problem of limited labeled data.

title: Automatic Pancreas Segmentation via Coarse Location and Ensemble Learning
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage pancreas segmentation framework: (1) coarse localization via superpixel classification using ResNet, and (2) fine segmentation using an ensemble of five U-Net variants trained with different loss functions (Dice, Focal, Jaccard, class-balanced CE, BCE) on 2.5D inputs, combined via averaging. Achieves Dice 84.10±4.91% and Jaccard 72.86±6.89% on the NIH pancreas dataset.

title: Improving Whole-Heart CT Image Segmentation by Attention Mechanism
architecture: 3D deeply supervised UNET with attention modules
organs: ["pulmonary artery", "ascending aorta", "right ventricular blood chamber", "right atrial blood chamber", "left ventricular blood chamber", "left atrial blood chamber", "myocardium of the left ventricle"]
main_contribution: Proposes three attention mechanisms (SNEM, AG, UCNet) and integrates them into a 3D deeply supervised UNET for whole-heart CT segmentation. Evaluates them individually and jointly, achieving a best Dice score of 0.9112, outperforming the baseline by 0.0302.

title: Cascade U-ResNets for Simultaneous Liver and Lesion Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a cascade U-ResNet architecture for simultaneous liver and lesion segmentation, investigates five loss functions for handling data imbalance, and demonstrates that ensembling models trained with different loss functions improves segmentation performance.

title: Automatic Segmentation Algorithm of Ultrasound Heart Image Based on Convolutional Neural Network and Image Saliency
main_contribution: Proposes two automatic segmentation algorithms for cardiac images: (1) a PET image segmentation method combining an improved Itti visual saliency model with an improved GrabCut algorithm, and (2) a CT image segmentation method using a convolutional neural network for heart localization and a stacked denoising autoencoder for pixel-level segmentation.

title: Channel-Attention U-Net: Channel Attention Mechanism for Semantic Segmentation of Esophagus and Esophageal Cancer
architecture: U-Net with Channel Attention Module (CAM) and Cross-level Feature Fusion Module (CFFM)
main_contribution: Proposes a Channel-Attention U-Net that integrates a Channel Attention Module (CAM) and a Cross-level Feature Fusion Module (CFFM) to improve segmentation of esophagus and esophageal cancer from CT slices, achieving IoU 0.625, Dice 0.732, and Hausdorff distance 3.193.

title: Eso-Net: A Novel 2.5D Segmentation Network With the Multi-Structure Response Filter for the Cancerous Esophagus
main_contribution: Proposes Eso-Net, a 2.5D segmentation network for automatic segmentation of the cancerous esophagus in CT images, incorporating a Multi-Structure Response Filter (MSRF) to extract 3D structural priors and Prior Attention Modules (PAM) to guide skip connections.

title: Automatic Segmentation Using a Hybrid Dense Network Integrated With an 3D-Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling Module for Computed Tomography (CT) Imaging
main_contribution: Proposes a 3D-ASPP module integrated with a 3D DenseNet encoder-decoder for volumetric segmentation of thoracic organs at risk from CT scans, achieving high Dice scores on SegTHOR 2019.

title: Cross-Dataset Multiple Organ Segmentation From CT Imagery Using FBP-Derived Domain Adaptation
organs: ["Left Lung", "Right Lung", "Left Kidney", "Right Kidney", "Left Psoas Muscle", "Right Psoas Muscle", "Liver", "Spleen"]
main_contribution: Proposes a filtered back-projection (FBP)-derived domain adaptation method to mitigate the discrepancy between CT datasets reconstructed with different kernels, improving cross-dataset multi-organ segmentation performance.

title: R2U3D: Recurrent Residual 3D U-Net for Lung Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes R2U3D, a recurrent residual 3D U-Net architecture for 3D lung segmentation, with variants including a dynamic recurrent unit and squeeze-and-excitation module. Achieves state-of-the-art performance on LUNA16 and VESSEL12 datasets using only 100 training scans without data augmentation.

title: Semi-Supervised Learning With Fact-Forcing for Medical Image Segmentation
organs: ["Pancreas", "Left Atrium", "Myocardium", "Left Ventricle", "Right Ventricle", "Intra-retinal Fluid", "Sub-retinal Fluid", "Pigment Epithelial Detachment"]
main_contribution: Proposes a semi-supervised learning method (FFSS) with a novel fact-forcing process that improves the quality of student feedback in a teacher-student framework, addressing the problem of low-quality feedback in existing pseudo-label-based methods.

title: 3D U-Net based method for fast segmentation of whole heart from CT images
main_contribution: Demonstrates that a properly trained NoNewNet (3D U-Net variant) using the NiftyNet framework achieves state-of-the-art whole heart segmentation on the MM-WHS CT dataset, and shows that reducing the border size during inference can speed up segmentation by over two orders of magnitude without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Segmentation of pathological liver tissue with Dilated Fully Convolutional Networks: A Preliminary Study
main_contribution: Proposes a dilated fully convolutional network (based on U-net) for liver and liver tumor segmentation in CT scans, using dilated convolutions to increase receptive field without losing resolution. Achieves mean Dice of 95.57% for liver and 59.36% for tumor on the MICCAI LiTS dataset.

title: End-to-End Supervised Lung Lobe Segmentation
organs: ["Lung lobes (5 lobes: right upper, right middle, right lower, left upper, left lower)"]
main_contribution: Proposes FRV-Net, a 3D fully convolutional neural network for end-to-end lung lobe segmentation from CT scans, incorporating multiple regularization techniques (Batch Normalization, Dropout, Deep Supervision, Multi-Task Learning) to handle small training datasets.

title: An Evaluation of CNN-based Liver Segmentation Methods using Multi-types of CT Abdominal Images from Multiple Medical Centers
main_contribution: Evaluates three well-known CNN architectures (CFCN, V-net, DRIU) for liver segmentation on a multi-center dataset including contrast-enhanced, non-contrast, and low-dose CT images, showing that performance degrades on low-dose and non-contrast images.

title: Preoperative Image Segmentation For Organ Visualization Using Augmented Reality Technology During Open Liver Surgery
main_contribution: Develops a U-net based deep learning method for automatic liver segmentation from CT scans, intended for 3D reconstruction and augmented reality visualization during open liver surgery.

title: Whole Heart Segmentation from CT images Using 3D U-Net architecture
organs: ["Left Ventricle (LV)", "Right Ventricle (RV)", "Left Atrium (LA)", "Right Atrium (RA)", "Pulmonary Artery (PA)", "Myocardium (Myo)", "Ascending Aorta (Aorta)"]
main_contribution: Proposes a 3D U-Net based framework for whole heart segmentation from CT images, with a novel data augmentation technique incorporating Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to improve training on small datasets.

title: Deep learning-based quantification of PET/CT prostate gland uptake: association with overall survival
main_contribution: Developed a deep learning algorithm for automated segmentation of the prostate gland on CT and quantification of 18F-choline PET uptake, and demonstrated that these automated biomarkers are significantly associated with overall survival in high-risk prostate cancer patients.

title: Analyzing Components of a Transformer under Different Dataset Scales in 3D Prostate CT Segmentation
main_contribution: Systematic analysis of components of a hybrid Transformer (nnFormer) for 3D prostate CT segmentation across multiple dataset scales, with fair parameter counts, showing that convolutions outperform Transformers at larger scales, pooling is better at small scales, and positional encodings provide negligible benefit.

title: Quantification of pulmonary involvement in COVID-19 pneumonia: an upgrade of the LungQuant software for lung CT segmentation
main_contribution: Presents LungQuant v2, an upgraded pipeline for automatic segmentation of lungs and COVID-19 lesions from CT scans, consisting of three DNNs (BB-net, U-net1, U-net2). Improvements include a bounding box network to handle variable FOVs, a new loss term to improve linearity with disease severity, and post-processing for left/right lung separation. The system achieves vDSC of 0.96 for lungs and 0.69 for lesions on an independent benchmark, with MAE of 2% for percentage of affected lung volume.

title: Deep Learning Segmentation Algorithms for X-ray CT data
main_contribution: The dissertation develops deep learning methods for semantic and instance segmentation of 3D CT data, with applications to industrial fiber-reinforced polymers and medical CT (liver, vessels). It introduces a novel 3D embedding learning approach for instance segmentation of fibers and a Mask Mining training strategy for liver and lesion segmentation.

title: Automatic liver segmentation in computed tomography scans using deep semantic segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a deep semantic segmentation CNN for automatic liver segmentation from CT scans, using data augmentation (rotation) and achieving 98.8% testing accuracy on a small dataset.

title: Establishment of normative spleen volume in a Japanese cohort using automated CT segmentation: diagnostic implications for liver fibrosis
main_contribution: Establishes population-specific reference values for spleen volume in healthy Japanese adults using deep learning-based segmentation, and develops a simple weight-based regression model to predict spleen volume. Defines Z-score thresholds for splenomegaly and evaluates their diagnostic utility for detecting liver fibrosis (cirrhosis) in an external cohort.

title: Heart and bladder detection and segmentation on FDG PET/CT by deep learning
main_contribution: Developed two 3D U-Net models to automatically segment heart and bladder on whole-body FDG PET/CT, aiming to suppress physiological FDG noise that can cause false positives in tumor detection. The models use multi-modal PET/CT input and achieve high Dice scores (0.96 for heart, 0.95 for bladder) on an independent test set.

title: Enhanced Cross-stage-attention U-Net for esophageal target volume segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes ECAU (Enhanced Cross-stage-attention U-Net) for automatic segmentation of esophageal GTV and CTV in simulated CT images, improving upon standard U-Net by replacing skip connections with cross-stage attention blocks.

title: A deep learning algorithm for automated adrenal gland segmentation on non-contrast CT images
main_contribution: Developed a deep learning model (nnU-Net) for automated adrenal gland segmentation on non-contrast CT, achieving high Dice scores (0.899-0.904) and applied it to a large-scale study of age-related adrenal volume changes in 2000 normal subjects.

title: Incremental 2D self-labelling for effective 3D medical volume segmentation with minimal annotations
main_contribution: Proposes an incremental 2D self-labelling framework that starts from a single annotated central slice per volume and iteratively propagates pseudo-labels to adjacent slices, fine-tuning a 2D U-Net to achieve 3D segmentation performance with minimal annotations.

title: Dosimetric impact of deep learning-based CT auto-segmentation on radiation therapy treatment planning for prostate cancer
main_contribution: Trained a 3D U-Net for prostate, bladder, and rectum segmentation on CT and evaluated both geometric and dosimetric impact on VMAT plans, showing that geometric performance is state-of-the-art but dosimetric analysis reveals deviations and no strong correlation between geometric and dosimetric metrics.

title: A deep image-to-image network organ segmentation algorithm for radiation treatment planning: principles and evaluation
main_contribution: Describes and evaluates a commercially available deep image-to-image network (DI2IN) algorithm for automatic contouring of organs at risk (lungs, heart, bladder, rectum) in CT for radiation treatment planning, demonstrating high agreement with manual contours.

title: Automated quantitative assessment of pediatric blunt hepatic trauma by deep learning-based CT volumetry
main_contribution: Developed an end-to-end deep learning framework for automated segmentation of liver and trauma regions in pediatric blunt hepatic trauma CT, enabling calculation of liver trauma volume and LPDI for severity assessment.

title: Advanced photon counting CT imaging pipeline for cardiac phenotyping of apolipoprotein E mouse models
main_contribution: Development of a comprehensive preclinical photon-counting CT (PCCT) imaging pipeline for cardiac phenotyping in mice, including deep learning-based left ventricle segmentation, and application to study APOE genotype effects on cardiac function.

title: Deep learning segmentation and registration-driven lung parenchymal volume and movement CT analysis in prone positioning
organs: ["Whole lung", "Right upper lobe", "Right middle lobe", "Right lower lobe", "Left upper lobe", "Left lower lobe"]
main_contribution: The study uses deep learning segmentation and deformable registration to quantify lung volume and movement changes between supine and prone positions, showing that prone positioning preferentially expands lower lobes and that fibrosis limits this expansion.

title: Improving segmentation precision in prostate cancer adaptive radiation therapy with a patient-specific network
main_contribution: Proposes a patient-specific network (PSN) framework for CTV segmentation in prostate cancer adaptive radiotherapy using CBCT, with two variants (PSNadaptive and PSNsequence) that continuously adapt to daily anatomical changes via sequential fine-tuning of a Swin UNETR model.

title: U-Net-based Pancreas Tumor Segmentation from Abdominal CT Images
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage U-Net framework for segmenting the pancreas and pancreatic tumors from abdominal CT images. The first U-Net segments the pancreas, and the second U-Net segments tumors within the masked pancreas region. The method uses Kaiming initialization, Leaky ReLU, and R2 regularization to improve performance.

title: Adaptive Three-Dimensional Identification of Renal Masses and Normal Kidney Tissues in Abdominal CT Using nnU-Net
main_contribution: Develops a 3D U-Net within the nnU-Net framework for automatic segmentation of kidneys, solid renal masses, and cystic renal masses in abdominal CT scans, achieving high accuracy (95.18%) and demonstrating clinical applicability.

title: Image analysis methods for identification and segmentation of biological structures using machine learning techniques
main_contribution: Developed a CNN-based organ localization and segmentation method for thoracic CT, incorporating spatial anatomical relationships and data augmentation.

title: Application of Medical Image 3D Visualization Web Platform in Auxiliary Diagnosis and Preoperative Planning
main_contribution: Development of a web-based 3D visualization platform for medical images that supports DICOM browsing, annotation, multiplanar reconstruction, volume rendering, lung parenchyma segmentation, and brain MRI analysis, with asynchronous reconstruction and model compression for efficient rendering.

title: ESP-UNet: Encoder-Decoder Convolutional Neural Network with Edge-Enhanced Features for Liver Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes ESP-UNet, a parallel UNet architecture that combines liver object segmentation with edge-enhanced border segmentation using Kirsch's filter, aiming to reduce under-segmentation and over-segmentation.

title: MAD-UNet: Multi-scale attention and deep supervision-based 3D UNet for automatic liver segmentation from CT
main_contribution: Proposes MAD-UNet, a 3D UNet architecture that integrates multi-scale attention and deep supervision for automatic liver segmentation from CT. The method replaces pooling with convolution, uses residual blocks, long-short skip connections (LSSC), and an attention module to aggregate multi-scale features, achieving high Dice scores on three public datasets.

title: Deep learning based clinical target volumes contouring and model adaptation for prostate cancer: easy and efficient application
main_contribution: Developed deep learning models for automatic contouring of clinical target volumes (CTV1 for pelvic lymph nodes, CTV2 for prostate/bed) in both radical and postoperative prostate cancer radiotherapy, and introduced a style adaptation method to personalize models to different physicians' contouring styles with only 10-20 cases.

title: MSAA-Net: A Multi-Scale Attention-Aware U-Net is Used to Segment the Liver
main_contribution: Proposes MSAA-Net, a U-Net variant that integrates Res2Net multi-scale feature extraction, SE blocks for channel recalibration, and a novel Multi-scale Attention Gate (MAG) to optimize skip connections, achieving high liver segmentation accuracy with reduced parameters.

title: DA-UNet: Deep supervision and atrous inception-based U-Net combining CRF for automatic liver segmentation from CT
main_contribution: Proposes DA-UNet, a 3D U-Net variant integrating residual blocks, an atrous inception module, deep supervision, and dense CRF post-processing for improved liver segmentation from CT scans.

title: Segmentation of Lung Lobes and Lesions in Chest CT for the Classification of COVID-19 Severity
main_contribution: Developed a deep learning pipeline combining 3D-UNet with pre-trained DenseNet169 for automatic segmentation of lung lobes and COVID-19 lesions, and calculation of total severity score (TSS) from CT scans.

title: Deep Learning for Automated Measurement of Total Cardiac Volume for Heart Transplantation Size Matching
main_contribution: First study to demonstrate automated measurement of Total Cardiac Volume (TCV) from CT scans using a 3D-CNN in a pediatric population, including subjects with congenital heart disease, achieving a mean Dice of 0.94 and mean absolute percent error of 5.5%.

title: Deep Learning-Based CT Splenic Segmentation and Morphometrics: A Spleen Volume Prediction Model
main_contribution: Developed a 3D U-Net model for automated spleen segmentation in CT, enabling quantitative measurement of volume, dimensions, and CT values, and derived a population-specific standard splenic volume (SSV) prediction formula for Chinese adults based on weight and body surface area.

title: Compare the Segmentation Accuracy of Heart Substructure on Contrast Enhanced CT by Deep Convolutional Neural Network with Different Loss Functions
organs: ["pericardium", "heart", "left atrium", "left ventricle", "right atrium", "right ventricle", "left main stem", "left anterior descending branch", "left circumflex branch", "right coronary artery"]
main_contribution: Systematically compares four deep learning models (GDL U-Net, WCEGDL U-Net, ELL U-Net, GDL V-Net) for automatic segmentation of 10 cardiac substructures on contrast-enhanced CT, showing that different loss functions yield varying performance across organs.

title: DALU-Net: Automated Liver Segmentation and Volumetry for Liver Transplantation in Abdominal Computed Tomography Volumes
main_contribution: Proposes DALU-Net, a deep attention convolutional LSTM network for automated liver segmentation and volumetry from abdominal CT, with evaluation on whole liver and individual lobes (left, right, caudate).

title: Comparison of Multi-Organ Segmentation Tools for Whole-Body [18F]FDG-PET/CT Clinical Imaging
main_contribution: This study compares two state-of-the-art automated multi-organ segmentation tools (MOOSE and TotalSegmentator) on a clinical NSCLC PET/CT dataset, using both technical (DSC) and clinical (SUVmax, HU) metrics against gold-standard manual delineation.

title: Development of an Integrated System for Automatic Tumor Detection for PET-CT Images
main_contribution: Development of a fully integrated AI system for automatic tumor detection in PET-CT images, comprising three subsystems: anatomical region classification, multi-organ segmentation, and tumor detection/segmentation. The system uses a standardization workflow to handle image variability and integrates with clinical PACS via DICOM.

title: The Efficacy of U-Net in Segmenting Liver Tumors from Abdominal CT Images
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage cascaded U-Net framework for liver and tumor segmentation from CT images, achieving competitive accuracy with minimal computational resources and training time.

title: A Weakly Reiterative Patches-Wise Framework for CT Liver and Lesions Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a weakly reiterative patches-wise framework for liver and lesion segmentation from CT scans, using two cascaded encoder-decoder networks: a localization network to extract ROI via Grad-CAMs, and a tuning network with multi-level patch learning, ASPP, and a custom multi-level loss function to refine boundaries and handle class imbalance.

title: Enhancing clinical efficiency and accuracy: automated segmentation for cervical cancer brachytherapy
main_contribution: Development and evaluation of a U-Net based automatic segmentation model for HR-CTV and pelvic OARs in cervical cancer brachytherapy, demonstrating good segmentation accuracy (average DSC 0.90 for HR-CTV, 0.85 for OARs) and significant time savings (AI-assisted delineation reduced manual time by ~50%).

title: 3D Visualization for Lung Surface Images of Covid-19 Patients based on U-Net CNN Segmentation
main_contribution: Develops a U-Net based CNN model for lung segmentation from CT scans and reconstructs 3D visualizations of lung surfaces to reveal erosion caused by Covid-19 infection, particularly peripheral GGO.

title: Coordinate-Unet 3D for segmentation of lung parenchyma
main_contribution: Proposes Coordinate-UNet 3D, a modified 3D UNet architecture with CoordConv and CGPD blocks, for accurate lung parenchyma segmentation from CT scans of NSCLC patients.

title: U-Net based frames partitioning and volumetric analysis for kidney detection in tomographic images
main_contribution: Proposes an automatic kidney detection system for CT images using U-Net with a novel frame partitioning strategy and volumetric coherent area analysis to reduce false positives and generate 3D kidney models.

title: Applying 3D U-Net Architecture to the Task of Multi-Organ Segmentation in Computed Tomography
main_contribution: Proposes a modified 3D U-Net for multi-organ segmentation of CT scans, achieving an average SDSC of 84.8% on a test set of 40 images across seven abdominal organs.

title: Cascaded Semantic Segmentation for Kidney and Tumor
main_contribution: Proposes a three-stage cascaded semantic segmentation pipeline for kidney and tumor segmentation from 3D CT images, achieving high Dice scores on the KiTS19 challenge test set.

title: Coarse to Fine Framework for Kidney Tumor Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a coarse-to-fine multi-resolution framework for automatic kidney and tumor segmentation in CT images, using an improved 3D U-Net with squeeze-excitation hybrid dilated convolutions (SE-HDC) and dual attention modules.

title: Fully Automatic Segmentation of Kidney and Tumor Based on Cascaded U-Nets
main_contribution: Proposes a cascaded 3D U-Net framework for automatic segmentation of kidney and renal tumor in CT images, where the first network segments the kidney as ROI and the second segments the tumor within that ROI.

title: Segmentation of Kidney and Renal Tumor in CT Scans Using Convolutional Networks
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage deep learning pipeline: a 2D AlexNet-based abdomen localizer to filter out non-ROI slices, followed by a 3D U-net for kidney and renal tumor segmentation. Achieves high Dice for kidney (0.9662) and moderate for tumor (0.7905) on KiTS19 cross-validation.

title: KiTS challenge: VNet with attention gates and deep supervision
main_contribution: Proposes a 3D fully convolutional network (VNet) with attention gates and deep supervision for automatic segmentation of kidney and kidney-tumor from CT scans, processing whole images without ROI cropping.

title: 3D Unet-based Kidney and Kidney Tumor Segmentation with Attentive Feature Learning
main_contribution: Proposes an attentive 3D U-Net based on nnU-Net for kidney and kidney tumor segmentation, incorporating a spatial attention module to improve feature representation, achieving a 1.5% improvement in segmentation accuracy on the validation set.

title: Automatic Kidney and Tumor Segmentation with Hybrid Hierarchical Networks
main_contribution: Proposes a fully automatic 3-step hierarchical framework combining 2D and 3D U-Net models for kidney and tumor segmentation in CT scans, achieving high Dice scores on the KiTS dataset.

title: KiTS19 Challenge Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage deep learning pipeline for kidney and tumor segmentation in CT scans: a ResUNet for coarse kidney ROI extraction and a DenseUNet for fine segmentation, using 2.5D convolutions to balance spatial context and computational efficiency.

title: Renal Tumor Segmentation in CT using Cascade U-Net with 2.5D approach
main_contribution: Proposes a Cascade U-Net with a 2.5D approach that combines multiple 2D U-Nets operating on different slice directions (z and y) and a two-step cascade (coarse localization then ROI refinement) to improve kidney and tumor segmentation in CT scans.

title: Using Two-stage Network to Segment Kidneys and Kidney Tumors
architecture: 3D U-Net variant with context and localization pathways
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage deep learning framework for automatic segmentation of kidneys and kidney tumors in CT images, consisting of a localization network followed by a segmentation network.

title: A Multi-scale Attention Network for Kidney Tumor Segmentation on CT Scans
main_contribution: Proposes a multi-scale attention network (MSAN) with an ensemble voting strategy for automatic kidney and tumor segmentation on CT scans.

title: Kidney and Kidney Tumor Segmentation Using Two-stage Convolutional Neural Network
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage CNN framework for kidney and kidney tumor segmentation: a 2.5D U-Net for kidney segmentation and a 3D U-Net for tumor segmentation, with multi-task learning (segmentation + regression) to improve performance.

title: Convolution Neural Network Application in Kidney Tumor Segmentation on CT Images
main_contribution: Proposes a novel network model similar to V-Net, combining Dense V-Net for kidney segmentation and Attention V-Net for tumor segmentation, with an ensembling strategy and preprocessing steps to improve dice.

title: Sequence and Spatial Feature Fusion for Kidney and Tumor Segmentation From CT Volumes
main_contribution: Proposes an encoder-decoder architecture that combines ConvLSTM layers in the encoder to capture inter-slice contextual information and 3D convolutional layers in the decoder to preserve spatial information, aiming to improve kidney and tumor segmentation from CT volumes.

title: Automatic Kidney and Tumor Segmentation with Attention-based V-Net
main_contribution: Proposes an attention-based V-Net architecture for automatic kidney and tumor segmentation from CT scans, incorporating a 3D decoupled spatial neural attention module.

title: Automatic system for the renal and cancer segmentation in CT images
main_contribution: Proposes a multi-stage system combining U-Net with post-processing (morphological operations, 3D model analysis, region growth, circularity) for automatic kidney and tumor segmentation in CT images.

title: Liver Segmentation on a Variety of CT Images Based on Convolutional Neural Networks Combined with Connected Components
main_contribution: The paper systematically evaluates the impact of applying a largest connected component (LCC) post-processing step to three CNN-based liver segmentation methods (FCN-CRF, DRIU, V-net) on a variety of CT image types (contrast-enhanced, low-dose contrast-enhanced, low-dose non-contrast). It demonstrates that LCC statistically significantly improves segmentation accuracy, particularly on low-dose and non-contrast images, while maintaining processing times under 10 seconds.

title: Kidney and Renal Tumor Segmentation by nnU-Net Using 3D CT Data from Different Sources
main_contribution: Systematically compares fine-tuning transfer learning vs. mixed dataset training for kidney and tumor segmentation using multi-source CT data, and proposes a data augmentation method that blends arterial and portal phase images. Also introduces an integration strategy combining results from two networks to improve overall segmentation.

title: Liver Tumors Segmentation Using 3D SegNet Deep Learning Approach
main_contribution: The paper proposes a 3D SegNet-based deep learning approach for liver tumor segmentation, but the actual implementation and evaluation focus on classification of liver disease stages (normal, compensated cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis, etc.) using CT and ultrasound images. The authors report high accuracy (up to 98.33%) for CNN-based classification.

title: Neural Network Based Whole Heart Segmentation from 3D CT Images
organs: ["Left Ventricle (LV)", "Myocardium of Left Ventricle (Myo)", "Right Ventricle (RV)", "Right Atrium (RA)", "Left Atrium (LA)", "Ascending Aorta (AA)", "Pulmonary Artery (PA)"]
main_contribution: Proposes a 3D U-Net based framework for whole heart segmentation from CT images, incorporating principal component analysis (PCA) as an additional data augmentation technique to improve performance on a small dataset.

title: Deep Learning-Based Computed Tomography Image Standardization to Improve Generalizability of Deep Learning-Based Hepatic Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a deep learning-based CT image standardization method using a GAN to convert various reconstructed CT images (FBP, IR, monoenergetic, etc.) to a target image (M80), thereby improving the performance of automated liver segmentation across different reconstruction protocols.

title: AutoPath: Image-Specific Inference for 3D Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes AutoPath, a reinforcement learning-based method that dynamically selects which residual blocks to use during inference for 3D segmentation, reducing computational cost while maintaining accuracy.

title: Preliminary Clinical Study of the Differences Between Interobserver Evaluation and Deep Convolutional Neural Network-Based Segmentation of Multiple Organs at Risk in CT Images of Lung Cancer
main_contribution: Evaluated the clinical performance of CNN-based auto-contouring for multiple OARs in lung cancer CT, comparing it to manual contouring by three observers, and assessed the impact of editing CNN-generated contours on time and accuracy.

title: Advanced Deep Learning Approach to Automatically Segment Malignant Tumors and Ablation Zone in the Liver With Contrast-Enhanced CT
main_contribution: Developed a deep learning pipeline using residual attention U-Net (RA-Unet) with transfer learning to automatically segment liver, liver tumors, and ablation zones in multi-phase (arterial and portal venous) CT images before and after ablation treatment. The method leverages the public LiTS dataset for pre-training and fine-tunes on a clinical dataset, achieving high Dice scores for liver and ablation zone segmentation and moderate performance for tumor segmentation.

title: Geometric and Dosimetric Evaluation of the Automatic Delineation of Organs at Risk (OARs) in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer Radiotherapy Based on a Modified DenseNet Deep Learning Network
main_contribution: Proposes a modified DenseNet-based deep learning model for automatic segmentation of six thoracic OARs in NSCLC CT images, and evaluates both geometric accuracy and dosimetric impact in radiotherapy planning.

title: Comprehensive clinical evaluation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation for radiotherapy in patients with cervical cancer
organs: ["stomach", "duodenum", "liver", "right kidney", "left kidney", "spinal cord", "cauda equina", "bowel bag", "bladder", "uterocervix", "anorectum", "right femoral head", "left femoral head", "CTV1_primary", "CTV2_pelvic node", "CTV3_para-aortic node"]
main_contribution: Developed and clinically evaluated a deep learning-based auto-segmentation model for 13 OARs and 3 CTVs in cervical cancer radiotherapy, using both geometric metrics (DSC, HD) and comprehensive clinical assessments (Turing test, inter-physician heterogeneity, contouring time reduction).

title: Validation of clinical acceptability of deep-learning-based automated segmentation of organs-at-risk for head-and-neck radiotherapy treatment planning
organs: ["42 organs-at-risk (OARs) including swallowing structures, mandible, mastoid, salivary glands, neurological organs, auditory structures, optical structures, carotid arteries, etc."]
main_contribution: Developed a deep learning model for autosegmentation of 42 organs-at-risk for head and neck cancer, and validated its clinical acceptability through a blinded randomized trial comparing DL-assisted workflow vs manual workflow. Demonstrated significant time savings (76% reduction) and improved geometric agreement with gold standard.

title: Clinical evaluation on automatic segmentation results of convolutional neural networks in rectal cancer radiotherapy
main_contribution: Comprehensive clinical evaluation of CNN-based auto-segmentation (DeepLabv3+ and ResUNet) for rectal cancer radiotherapy, comparing geometric accuracy (volumetric and surface DSC) and dosimetric impact (replanning with auto-segmented structures) against ground truth and ABAS.

title: Clinical target volume and organs at risk segmentation for rectal cancer radiotherapy using the Flex U-Net network
main_contribution: Proposes Flex U-Net, a deep learning framework that integrates a register network to correct noise in manual annotations, improving CTV and OAR segmentation for rectal cancer radiotherapy.

title: Applying a novel two-step deep learning network to improve the automatic delineation of esophagus in non-small cell lung cancer radiotherapy
main_contribution: Proposes a two-step deep learning framework for automatic segmentation of thoracic OARs, with a specific focus on improving esophagus delineation. The first step uses DenseNet67 to segment five OARs, and the second step uses a residual attention network on a cropped region around the trachea to refine the esophagus segmentation. The method is evaluated both geometrically (DSC, HD95, ASD) and dosimetrically (IMRT plan comparison).

title: TriSwinUNETR lobe segmentation model for computing DIR-free CT-ventilation

title: Deep Learning-Augmented Head and Neck Organs at Risk Segmentation From CT Volumes

main_contribution: Proposes SEB-Net, a deep learning framework that combines a Siamese ensemble strategy with shared weights across three orthogonal CT planes and a boundary loss to improve segmentation accuracy of head and neck organs at risk, particularly small organs.

title: Automatic Lung Segmentation and Quantification of Aeration in Computed Tomography of the Chest Using 3D Transfer Learning
main_contribution: Development of a 3D U-net based algorithm for automatic lung segmentation in CT scans, using transfer learning from animal (pig) to human data, enabling quantification of lung volumes, aeration compartments, and lung recruitability in pathological conditions.

title: A deep learning model for CT-based kidney volume determination in dogs and normal reference definition
main_contribution: First deep learning model for automatic kidney detection and volume estimation from CT scans in dogs, along with establishment of reference ranges for normal kidney volume considering body weight and body condition score.

title: Study on the adoption of an artificial intelligence algorithm for the automatic segmentation of visceral organs.
architecture: Total Segmentator (nnU-Net based) and MONAI Label
main_contribution: The study evaluates the use of pre-trained AI segmentation tools (Total Segmentator, MONAI Label) for automatic segmentation of thoraco-abdominal organs, focusing on segmentation time and reproducibility across two different workstations.

title: A 3D U-NET BASED ON EARLY FUSION MODEL: IMPROVEMENT, COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS WITH STATE-OF-THE-ART MODELS AND FINE-TUNING
organs: ["Spleen", "Right kidney", "Left kidney", "Esophagus", "Gallbladder", "Liver", "Stomach", "Aorta", "Inferior vena cava", "Portal and splenic vein", "Pancreas", "Right adrenal gland", "Left adrenal gland"]
main_contribution: Proposes a fine-tuned 3D U-Net based early fusion model that combines HSV and grayscale color spaces for multi-organ segmentation of abdominal CT images, with hyperparameter optimization and comparison against state-of-the-art models.

title: Deep Learning-Based Adrenal Gland Volumetry for the Prediction of Diabetes
main_contribution: Developed a 3D nnU-Net model for automated adrenal gland segmentation and volumetry from CT scans, and demonstrated that adrenal gland volume (AGV) is associated with current glycemic status and predicts incident type 2 diabetes in a large longitudinal cohort.

title: PAFU-Net: A Pyramidal Attention-Fortified U-Net for Precise Liver Segmentation in Abdominal CT scans
main_contribution: Proposes PAFU-Net, a lightweight U-Net variant integrating ASPP-gated skip connections, channel attention in encoder, CBAM at bottleneck, and spatial attention in decoder for precise liver segmentation from CT scans.

title: Feasibility of artificial intelligence-driven interfractional monitoring of organ changes by mega-voltage computed tomography in intensity-modulated radiotherapy of prostate cancer
main_contribution: Demonstrated the feasibility of using a commercial AI-based FC-DenseNet model for auto-segmentation of organs-at-risk (body, rectal balloon, bladder+prostate) on low-quality daily MVCT images in prostate cancer radiotherapy, achieving high Dice scores (>0.88) and low mean surface distances (<1.43 mm). Also showed the model's utility for interfractional monitoring of organ changes across six MVCT scans.

title: 2.5D cascaded context-based network for liver and tumor segmentation from CT images
main_contribution: Proposes CCLNet, a 2.5D network combining cascaded context module (CCM) and Ladder Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (L-ASPP) for automatic liver and tumor segmentation from CT, balancing accuracy and computational cost.

title: An improved residual U-Net with morphological-based loss function for automatic liver segmentation in computed tomography
main_contribution: Proposes an improved residual U-Net (iResU-Net) for liver CT segmentation, incorporating residual modules, batch normalization, a Dice-based loss with morphological weighting, and data augmentation. Also extends the method to 3D.

title: Multi-scale attention and deep supervision-based 3D UNet for automatic liver segmentation from CT
main_contribution: Proposes MAD-UNet, a 3D UNet variant that integrates multi-scale attention and deep supervision for automatic liver segmentation from CT. The network replaces pooling with convolution, uses residual blocks, long-short skip connections (LSSC), and an attention module to aggregate multi-scale features, while applying deep supervision with a combined BCE and Dice loss.

title: Hierarchical volumetric transformer with comprehensive attention for medical image segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a novel 3D segmentation framework that hierarchically integrates convolution, transformer, and attention mechanisms, including a double transformer structure, local multi-channel attention (LMCA), and global multi-scale attention (GMSA) with deep supervision.

title: Liver Segmentation: A Weakly End-to-End Supervised Model
main_contribution: Proposes an end-to-end liver segmentation model based on an improved SegCaps network, incorporating selective preprocessing, data augmentation, and post-processing to handle limited annotated data.

title: Feasibility of artificial intelligence-based decision supporting system in tolvaptan prescription for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
main_contribution: Developed a fully automated 3D segmentation model (3D Dynamic U-Net) for total kidney volume (TKV) measurement in ADPKD patients, achieving a Dice score of 0.979 after post-processing, and integrated it into a SaaS platform for tolvaptan prescription decision support based on Mayo imaging classification.

title: Prediction of recipient renal function in living donor kidney transplantation using baseline characteristics and donor renal cortex volume
main_contribution: Developed a 3D U-Net-based automated segmentation model for donor kidney cortex volume from CT scans, and integrated this volume into a predictive model (GAM) for recipient post-transplant eGFR.

title: Region segmentation for lung cancer Computed Tomography image using 3D U-Net model
main_contribution: The paper presents a 3D U-Net-based framework for automated lung segmentation from CT scans using the MSD Task06_Lung dataset, achieving a Dice score of 0.67 and high precision/recall (0.99).

title: Artificial intelligence – assisted three-dimensional preoperative planning in liver tumor surgery: a comparative real-world study
main_contribution: The study evaluates the clinical effectiveness of the HepatoScan AI system, which integrates neural network-based CT segmentation and interactive 3D preoperative modeling, in a real-world comparative setting. It demonstrates improved diagnostic sensitivity and favorable intraoperative outcomes in patients with liver tumors, particularly in anatomically complex cases (TROPH-L II–III).

title: Efficient Liver Segmentation using Advanced 3D-DCNN Algorithm on CT Images
main_contribution: Proposes a 3D-DCNN combined with iterative region growing for liver segmentation from CT images, with preprocessing and feature extraction.

title: Spatial Aggregation of Holistically-Nested Convolutional Neural Networks for Automated Pancreas Localization and Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage cascaded deep learning framework for pancreas localization and segmentation using holistically-nested convolutional networks (HNNs) on three orthogonal views. Localization uses multi-view max-pooled HNN probability maps to generate a bounding box, and segmentation combines interior and boundary cues via superpixel aggregation with random forests. Achieves state-of-the-art DSC of 81.27% on 82 CT scans with 4-fold cross-validation.

title: 3D Anisotropic Hybrid Network: Transferring Convolutional Features from 2D Images to 3D Anisotropic Volumes
main_contribution: Proposes a 3D Anisotropic Hybrid Network (AH-Net) that transfers convolutional features from a 2D pre-trained network to 3D anisotropic volumes, enabling effective learning from limited 3D data while exploiting between-slice context. Achieves state-of-the-art results on DBT lesion detection and CT liver/liver tumor segmentation.

title: Fully Automated Organ Segmentation in Male Pelvic CT Images
main_contribution: Presents a fully automated deep learning workflow for multi-organ segmentation (prostate, bladder, rectum, femoral heads) in male pelvic CT scans, combining a 2D localization network and a 3D segmentation network with ResNeXt blocks.

title: Deep Sequential Segmentation of Organs in Volumetric Medical Scans
main_contribution: Proposes Sensor3D, a U-Net-like architecture with bidirectional C-LSTM and time-distributed layers that processes volumetric scans sequentially, enabling segmentation of slabs of slices without requiring full volume input, thus overcoming memory and resizing limitations.

title: Organ at Risk Segmentation in Head and Neck CT Images Using a Two-Stage Segmentation Framework Based on 3D U-Net

This approach improves accuracy, especially for small organs, and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the MICCAI 2015 Challenge dataset.

title: CYLINDRICAL TRANSFORM: 3D SEMANTIC SEGMENTATION OF KIDNEYS WITH LIMITED ANNOTATED IMAGES
architecture: AlexNet, GoogLeNet (classification DCNNs) with cylindrical transform; also FCNs (GoogLeNet, VGG-19) for comparison

title: Comparison of U-net-based Convolutional Neural Networks for Liver Segmentation in CT
architecture: U-Net (2D and 3D variants), ensemble of orthogonal 2D U-Nets
main_contribution: Systematic comparison of 2D and 3D U-net variants for liver segmentation in CT, including a novel ensemble of three orthogonal 2D U-nets that outperforms single 2D and 3D approaches under hardware constraints.

title: Accurate Congenital Heart Disease Model Generation for 3D Printing
main_contribution: Proposes a framework combining deep learning (3D U-net and 2D U-net) with graph matching for fully automated whole heart and great vessel segmentation in congenital heart disease (CHD) CT images, addressing the large structural variations typical of CHD.

title: A Method of Rapid Quantification of Patient-Specific Organ Dose for CT Using Coupled Deep-Learning based Multi-Organ Segmentation and GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo Dose Computing
main_contribution: First study to combine deep-learning-based multi-organ segmentation with GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo dose calculation for rapid patient-specific CT organ dose assessment, achieving clinically acceptable accuracy and efficiency.

title: 3D Kidneys and Kidney Tumor Semantic Segmentation using Boundary-Aware Networks
main_contribution: Proposes an end-to-end 3D boundary-aware CNN for kidney and kidney tumor segmentation, incorporating a dedicated boundary stream supervised by edge-aware losses.

title: Unpaired Multi-modal Segmentation via Knowledge Distillation
organs: ["left ventricle myocardium", "left atrium blood cavity", "left ventricle blood cavity", "ascending aorta", "liver", "spleen", "right kidney", "left kidney"]

title: Patient-specific finetuning of deep learning models for adaptive radiotherapy in prostate CT
main_contribution: Proposes a patient-specific fine-tuning approach for CNN-based segmentation in adaptive radiotherapy, where the model is adapted using imaging from previous treatment fractions to improve segmentation of daily CT scans.

title: MetricUNet: Synergistic Image- and Voxel-Level Learning for Precise Prostate Segmentation via Online Sampling
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage framework for CT prostate segmentation, with a multi-task UNet that integrates online voxel-wise metric learning to improve feature representation and boundary delineation.

title: Lung Segmentation and Nodule Detection in Computed Tomography Scan using a Convolutional Neural Network Trained Adversarially using Turing Test Loss
architecture: Modified SUMNet (encoder VGG16) for segmentation; LeNet for classification
main_contribution: Proposes a computationally efficient two-stage framework for lung segmentation and nodule detection in CT scans. Stage 2 uses a LeNet-based classifier on patches extracted from the segmented lung region to detect nodules.

title: Generalizable Cone Beam CT Esophagus Segmentation using Physics-Based Data Augmentation
main_contribution: Developed a physics-based data augmentation method that generates synthetic CBCTs (sCBCTs) from planning CTs by extracting scatter artifacts using Power-Law Adaptive Histogram Equalization (PL-AHE) and reconstructing with CBCT parameters. This enables training a 3D-UNet that generalizes across both pCT and CBCT for esophagus segmentation.

title: 3D Graph Anatomy Geometry-Integrated Network for Pancreatic Mass Segmentation, Diagnosis, and Quantitative Patient Management
main_contribution: Proposes a novel Segmentation-Mesh-Classification Network (SMCN) that integrates 3D anatomy geometry with deep learning for pancreatic mass segmentation, differential diagnosis, and patient management using multi-phase CT. It is the first work to address the full-spectrum taxonomy of ten pancreatic mass types.

title: Multi-class probabilistic atlas-based whole heart segmentation method in cardiac CT and MRI
main_contribution: Proposes a probabilistic atlas-based whole heart segmentation framework using non-rigid registration and Bayesian inference, achieving state-of-the-art performance on the MM-WHS-2017 dataset (mVOE 14.5% for CT).

title: A Deep-Learning Approach For Direct Whole-Heart Mesh Reconstruction
main_contribution: Proposes an end-to-end deep learning method that directly predicts whole-heart surface meshes from volumetric CT and MR images using graph convolutional networks, deforming template spheres to match cardiac structures, avoiding voxel-wise segmentation and post-processing.

title: Evaluation of Preprocessing Techniques for U-Net Based Automated Liver Segmentation
main_contribution: Systematically evaluates the impact of various preprocessing techniques (HU windowing, CLAHE, z-score normalization, median filtering, BM3D) individually and in combination on U-Net-based liver segmentation from CT scans, identifying the optimal combination (HU windowing + median filtering + z-score) achieving 90.84% Dice on test data.

title: Liver Segmentation in Time-resolved C-arm CT Volumes Reconstructed from Dynamic Perfusion Scans using Time Separation Technique

title: Fully Automatic Segmentation of Gross Target Volume and Organs-at-Risk for Radiotherapy Planning of Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
main_contribution: Proposes a fully automatic pipeline for segmentation of 45 OARs and 2 GTVs in NPC CT images, using nnU-Net with intensity harmonization and cropping preprocessing.

title: Full-body deep learning-based automated contouring of contrast-enhanced murine organs for small animal irradiator CBCT
main_contribution: Development of a deep learning model combined with iodine-based contrast enhancement to automatically segment abdominal, thoracic, and skeletal organs in low-quality CBCT scans from a small animal irradiator, achieving high accuracy and speed (<1 second).

title: Deep-learning Segmentation of Small Volumes in CT images for Radiotherapy Treatment Planning

title: An Automated Deep Learning-Based Software for Total Lung Volume Calculation and Lung 3D Model Reconstruction
main_contribution: Development of an automated deep learning-based software for lung segmentation, 3D reconstruction, and total lung volume (TLV) calculation using a modified BCDU-Net, with a Vietnamese-language interface.

title: An Efficient Deep Learning Approach for Liver Segmentation in Medical Imaging
main_contribution: Development of a 3D U-Net-based deep learning model for automated liver segmentation from volumetric CT scans, using a custom composite loss function (AdvancedComboLoss) and a standardized preprocessing pipeline.

title: Speed-Accuracy-Memory Cooperative Optimization of Lightweight Dynamic 3D U-Net for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a lightweight dynamic 3D U-Net that combines deformable convolutions and a dynamic weight mechanism to achieve collaborative optimization of speed, accuracy, and memory usage for medical image segmentation, specifically liver CT segmentation.

title: HATN: hierarchical adaptive transformer network for real-time medical image segmentation using hybrid CNN-ViT architecture with multi-scale attention and uncertainty-aware loss functions
main_contribution: Proposes HATN, a hybrid CNN-ViT architecture combining Swin-Transformer encoder, Multi-Scale Deformable Attention (MSDA) bottleneck, Multi-Scale Channel Attention (MSCA) skip connections, and Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty estimation, trained with a compound uncertainty-aware loss. title: Comparative Analysis of Baseline Vnet and Unet Architectures on Pancreas Segmentation
main_contribution: A comparative analysis of baseline Unet and Vnet architectures for pancreas segmentation on the NIH-CT82 dataset, reporting training/validation accuracy and loss.

title: Dual-Scale Transformer-Guided Attention Network for Efficient Multi-OAR Segmentation in Head and Neck Radiotherapy
organs: ["Brainstem", "Mandible", "Left Parotid", "Right Parotid", "Left Optic Nerve", "Right Optic Nerve", "Optic Chiasm", "Pituitary Gland", "Left Lens", "Right Lens", "and other OARs (total 22 on HNSCC, 9 on MICCAI)"]
main_contribution: Proposes DSTANet, a dual-scale transformer-guided attention network for multi-OAR segmentation in head and neck CT, achieving high accuracy and efficiency.

title: Liver Segmentation in CT Images Using Residual U-Net and 3D CRF
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage liver segmentation method for CT images: first using a modified Residual U-Net (with ResNet-D and scSE blocks) for 2D slice segmentation, then applying 3D Conditional Random Field (CRF) to incorporate 3D context and refine boundaries.

title: Onco-Seg: Adapting Promptable Concept Segmentation for Multi-Modal Medical Imaging
architecture: SAM3 (Segment Anything Model 3) with LoRA adaptation
main_contribution: Adapts Meta's SAM3 foundation model for multi-modal medical image segmentation using LoRA fine-tuning, trained on 35 datasets (98,000+ cases) and evaluated on 12 benchmarks, with two clinical deployment patterns.

title: Portable framework to deploy deep learning segmentation models for medical images
main_contribution: Development of an open-source, portable framework for deploying deep learning segmentation models in medical imaging, integrated with CERR, supporting multiple programming languages (MATLAB, Octave, Python) and operating systems via Singularity containers and Conda environments.

title: Current State of Community-Driven Radiological AI Deployment in Medical Imaging
main_contribution: This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the current state of community-driven AI deployment in radiology, highlighting barriers, integration points, and real-world use cases. It introduces a taxonomy of AI use cases and demonstrates how open-source tools like MONAI Deploy can facilitate standards-based deployment in clinical workflows.

title: MONAI: An open-source framework for deep learning in healthcare
main_contribution: Introduces MONAI, an open-source, community-supported PyTorch-based framework for deep learning in healthcare, providing domain-optimized tools for medical imaging, including network architectures, transforms, loss functions, and workflows.

title: U-Mamba: Enhancing Long-range Dependency for Biomedical Image Segmentation
organs: ["liver", "spleen", "pancreas", "right kidney", "left kidney", "stomach", "gallbladder", "esophagus", "aorta", "inferior vena cava", "right adrenal gland", "left adrenal gland", "duodenum"]
main_contribution: Proposes U-Mamba, a hybrid CNN-SSM architecture that combines local feature extraction of CNNs with long-range dependency modeling of Mamba (SSM) for biomedical image segmentation, achieving superior performance over CNN and Transformer baselines on multiple tasks.

title: VISTA3D: A Unified Segmentation Foundation Model For 3D Medical Imaging
main_contribution: VISTA3D is a unified 3D segmentation foundation model that supports automatic segmentation of 127 classes, interactive segmentation with point clicks, zero-shot segmentation of novel classes, and few-shot finetuning. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on both automatic and interactive tasks across 14 datasets.

title: nnInteractive: Redefining 3D Promptable Segmentation
main_contribution: Introduces nnInteractive, the first comprehensive 3D interactive open-set segmentation model supporting diverse prompts (points, scribbles, boxes, lasso) and trained on 120+ multimodal datasets, integrated into Napari and MITK.

title: Evaluation of Deep Learning to Augment Image-Guided Radiotherapy for Head and Neck and Prostate Cancers
architecture: 3D U-Net variant (CNN), trained as an ensemble
organs: ["prostate gland", "seminal vesicles", "bladder", "rectum", "left femur", "right femur", "brainstem", "mandible", "spinal cord", "left parotid gland", "right parotid gland", "left submandibular gland", "right submandibular gland", "left globe", "right globe"]
main_contribution: Multi-site (8 hospitals, 761 CTs) clinical evaluation of a 3D U-Net ensemble autocontouring system covering 15 OARs across prostate and head-and-neck radiotherapy, achieving Fleiss κ within expert interobserver variability for 14 of 15 structures and near-identical Dice on held-out-site and public external data. Clinically, correcting autocontours cut contouring time by a mean of 93% (4.98 min/scan H&N, 3.40 min/scan prostate vs 73–87 min manual). Distinctively, it ships as an open-source end-to-end workflow (Microsoft InnerEye: Gateway anonymization, Azure ML training, cloud segmentation service, correction tool) designed for direct PACS integration rather than as a novel architecture.

Proposes DMSAN, a UNet variant whose encoder is built from Res2Net (R2N) multi-scale bottleneck blocks with inter-stage high/low-resolution feature fusion and a sigmoid-attention recalibration of skip connections, trained end-to-end with dice loss for liver segmentation. Achieves DSC 0.973 on 3DIRCADb and 0.964 on the independent CHAOS test set (leaderboard-verified), with an ablation showing scale factor s=4 is optimal. Incremental architectural contribution (R2N + attention applied to a UNet) with medium methodological rigor and no released code.

title: Liver tumor segmentation based on 3D convolutional neural network with dual scale
main_contribution: The paper proposes TDP-CNN, a dual-path 3D CNN that fuses high-resolution local features (43^3 patches) with subsampled global context (129^3 patches) via additive feature fusion, using a 1x1x1 convolution in the fully connected stage to preserve spatial information and FC-CRF postprocessing to remove false positives. On LiTS it achieved liver Dice 0.965 (rank 1) and tumor Dice 0.689 (rank 2) against all MICCAI 2017 challenge entries, while demonstrating that patch-size scaling monotonically improves 3D segmentation performance up to 43^3. The main limitation is weak small-tumor segmentation (<500 voxels) and high computational cost (96h training, 13.3 min/volume inference).

title: Automatic segmentation and applicator reconstruction for CT-based brachytherapy of cervical cancer using 3D convolutional neural networks
organs: ["HR-CTV", "bladder", "small intestine", "sigmoid", "rectum", "intrauterine tube", "left ovoid tube", "right ovoid tube", "left ovoid", "right ovoid", "cervical stopper"]
main_contribution: This is the first study to apply 3D CNNs to CT-based cervical cancer brachytherapy, introducing DSD-UNET - a 3D U-Net enhanced with residual blocks, multi-rate dilated convolutions, deep supervision, and dual-channel (original + CLAHE-enhanced) input - which outperformed 3D U-Net on all structures (mean DSC: 86.9% bladder, 82.9% HR-CTV, 82.1% rectum, but only 64.5% sigmoid). It further presents the first fully automatic applicator reconstruction pipeline, combining DSD-UNET component segmentation with 3D skeletonization and fifth-degree polynomial curve fitting to achieve sub-millimetre channel-path accuracy (mean HD <1 mm) in ~22 s per case without manual intervention. While clinically motivated and methodologically detailed, the single-center dataset (n=91), CPU-only training, absence of external validation, and weak small-bowel structure segmentation temper generalizability.

The key contribution is demonstrating that a SegNet fine-tuned exclusively on portal-venous phase CT robustly segments the liver across all four CT phases (plain, arterial, PV, delayed), with per-phase quantitative evidence — addressing the gap that most liver CAD work is single-phase. Second, a power-law transformation-based multi-branch contrast enhancement combined with K-means clustering segments liver tumors without DL training, achieving DC 85.07%, presented as a practical alternative to data-hungry tumor CNNs. Main limitation is a high false-positive rate in tumor segmentation (TPR 76.65%) on a small 10-patient single-center test set.

title: Deep learning of the sectional appearances of 3D CT images for anatomical structure segmentation based on an FCN voting method
architecture: FCN (fully convolutional network) with VGG16 backbone
organs: ["right lung", "left lung", "heart", "aorta", "esophagus", "liver", "gallbladder", "stomach and duodenum (2nd portion)", "stomach/duodenum lumen", "contents inside stomach and duodenum", "spleen", "right kidney", "left kidney", "inferior vena cava", "portal vein/splenic vein/superior mesenteric vein", "pancreas", "bladder", "prostate", "uterus"]
main_contribution: Zhou et al. propose a single 2D fully convolutional network (VGG16-based FCN, fine-tuned from ImageNet weights) that segments 19 torso structures in 3D CT via a 3D-2D-3D transformation: 2D sections are sampled in three orthogonal planes, segmented pixel-to-label, stacked back to 3D, and fused by voxel-wise majority voting with a largest-organ-volume tie-break. The key novelty is that one 2D network trained on ~100,000 sections from 240 annotated CT scans handles arbitrary scan ranges and heterogeneous acquisitions without 3D convolutions or per-organ models, achieving 87.9% voxel labeling accuracy on 12 held-out test scans. The work is an early (2017) demonstration of transfer-learning-based multi-organ segmentation, but evaluation is limited to a single aggregate, background-inclusive accuracy metric on a small single-center test set with no baseline comparisons.

This paper presents DDCNN, a 2D fully convolutional network built on VGG-16 with novel dual-path dilated convolution modules that inject multi-scale low-level context directly from the input image and high-level context at the network's end, and reports the first CNN-based auto-segmentation of both CTV and OARs in planning CT for rectal cancer radiotherapy. DDCNN outperformed U-Net by 3.8% average DSC (e.g., CTV 87.7% vs 81.9%; bladder 93.4% vs 91.2%) while segmenting all structures in ~45 seconds per patient, with degraded but still useful results for intestine (65.3%) and colon (61.8%). The work demonstrated clinically relevant speed and robustness to body habitus, though validation was limited to a single institution with DSC as the only accuracy metric.

title: Deep-Learning Convolutional Neural Network: Inner and Outer Bladder Wall Segmentation in CT Urography
main_contribution: This work extends DL-CNN-guided cascaded level sets from whole-bladder segmentation to separate inner and outer bladder wall contours in CT urography, introducing an '8×8 jittering' ROI labeling scheme to handle the very thin bladder wall and integrating the CNN likelihood map only into the fourth cascade stage. On 172 CTU scans it achieves ~87-90% volume intersection for both walls on the test set, significantly outperforming the non-DL CLASS system, ITK-SNAP, and the authors' prior whole-bladder DL-CNN (p<0.01). It is a methodological stepping stone toward bladder lesion detection/CAD rather than a generic multi-organ segmentation advance, and notably lacks Dice reporting, external validation, and code release.

title: U-Net-based Deep-Learning Bladder Segmentation in CT Urography
main_contribution: Developed U-Net-based 2D and 3D deep-learning bladder segmentation (U-DL) for CT urography that eliminates the user-input bounding box and level-set postprocessing required by the authors' prior DCNN-LS. Systematic ablation of dimensionality, resolution, and cropping found the 2D U-DL at full resolution with automated cropping best, improving AJI from 76.2% to 85.0% on a 92-case independent test set (p<0.001) and outperforming two non-DL baselines. Notable negative finding for this review: the 3D variant underperformed 2D, attributed to only 81 training volumes versus 7,629 slice samples.

title: Deep convolutional neural network for segmentation of thoracic organs-at-risk using cropped 3D images
architecture: 3D U-Net (cascaded: multi-label localization network + individual binary organ segmentation networks)
main_contribution: This paper introduces a cascaded framework that decouples organ localization (multi-label 3D U-Net on downsampled, center-cropped volumes) from per-organ binary segmentation (specialized 3D U-Nets on randomly-margin-cropped patches), making full-resolution 3D thoracic CT segmentation feasible within GPU memory limits, complemented by a novel test-time augmentation based on multiple randomized croppings. It ranked 1st (ongoing phase) and 2nd (live phase) in the 2017 AAPM Thoracic Auto-segmentation Challenge (Dice 0.972-0.979 lungs, 0.925 heart, 0.893 cord, 0.726 esophagus), surpassing inter-rater reference for lungs/cord, and generalized to an independent institutional dataset while reducing clinical contour editing to ~7.5 min/patient. It is a landmark demonstration that crop-based cascaded 3D U-Nets can achieve challenge-winning, clinically translatable multi-OAR segmentation for radiation therapy planning.

title: Automatic Liver Segmentation by Integrating Fully Convolutional Networks into Active Contour Models
architecture: FCN-8s integrated into active contour models (ACM)
