main_contribution: This paper proposes a hybrid deep-learning/deformable-model framework in which a single modified FCN-8s predicts a 7-category layered label map (encoding interior/exterior region and distance-to-boundary bands derived from signed distance transforms), which is converted into an adaptive external steering force for a localizing region-based active contour model with sparse-field level-set evolution. The force's distance-adaptive magnitude and position-dependent direction enable initialization far from the liver boundary, boundary smoothness enforcement, topology preservation, and elimination of spurious fragments. Without fine-tuning, the method generalizes to two external datasets (Dice 96.2% SLIVER07, 94.3% LiTS), consistently improving over FCN alone (~94%), though it remains 2D slice-based and lacks comparison with contemporary deep learning SOTA.

The paper proposes a Boosting-inspired cascaded ensemble of three 2D patch-based ResNet18 classifiers for OAR segmentation (parotids, thyroid, optic nerves) in NPC planning CTs, where each subsequent network is trained on patches filtered by its predecessors to concentrate on error-prone samples, with final labels decided by majority voting. On 140 single-center patients it outperforms FCN-8s, U-Net, DeepLab-v3, and a single voxelwise ResNet (mean DSC ~92% parotid, ~92% thyroid, ~89-90% optic nerve), and ablations show the framework is backbone-agnostic since deeper/wider backbones add no benefit. The approach remains 2D without 3D spatial context and has slow pixel-wise inference, limiting its fit as a fully '3D' segmentation method for this review.

title: Automatic multi-organ segmentation in dual-energy CT (DECT) with dedicated 3D fully convolutional DECT networks
architecture: 3D fully convolutional network (3D U-Net-based) with four dual-energy fusion variants: LC-net (linear combination), MC-net (multi-channel), MI-net (multi-image/two-branch), and late fusion
main_contribution: This paper presents the first systematic investigation of information-fusion strategies for deep-learning-based DECT segmentation, proposing four 3D fully convolutional architectures that fuse the two spectral images at image level (LC-net, MC-net), mid-feature level (MI-net), or output level (late fusion), plus residual-block variants. The feature-level fusion MI-net proved best (Dice ~92–98% per organ; +2–6% over single-energy 3D U-Net), demonstrating that learnable joint spectral feature extraction — requiring neither predefined fusion weights nor organ/energy-specific priors — exploits dual-energy information more effectively than linear combination. Secondary contributions include a weighted multi-class Dice loss with median-frequency balancing and boundary compensation, a manifold-learning-based data-partitioning scheme for small cohorts, and a transparent analysis of patch-based training limitations, though results rest on a small (45-volume), single-center dataset with internal cross-validation only.

title: Improving the Slice Interaction of 2.5D CNN for Automatic Pancreas Segmentation
architecture: Two-stage coarse-to-fine: cascaded 3D V-Nets (localization) + 2.5D Slice Interaction Network (SINet) with Slice Correlation Module (refinement)
main_contribution: The paper proposes a two-stage coarse-to-fine pancreas segmentation framework whose refinement network (SINet) preserves the 2.5D slice structure through all encoder/decoder levels, combined with a bilinear-pooling Slice Correlation Module for non-local cross-slice attention and a slice-shuffle self-supervised pre-training task. A Square Root Dice loss boosts localization recall by up-weighting misclassified foreground voxels. The method achieves state-of-the-art 86.21±4.37% Dice on NIH Pancreas-CT under 4-fold cross-validation, with ensemble fusion and recurrent refinement.

title: Complete Abdomen and Pelvis Segmentation using U-Net Variant Architecture
architecture: 3D U-Net variant with pre-activation residual blocks
organs: ["liver", "spleen", "left/right kidneys", "pancreas", "left/right adrenal glands", "left/right renal arteries", "left/right renal veins", "diaphragm", "bladder", "uterus/prostate", "lumbar intervertebral discs (T12-S1)", "aorta", "inferior vena cava", "spinal column", "stomach", "small bowel", "large bowel", "gallbladder", "subcutaneous adipose tissue", "visceral adipose tissue", "muscle", "bone", "connective tissue/small vessels"]
main_contribution: Presents a 3D U-Net variant (pre-activation residual blocks, RReLU, instance norm) with prevalence-weighted Dice loss performing whole abdomen/pelvis segmentation into 33 structures — the largest structure count reported at the time — including tissues typically ignored (adipose, muscle, connective tissue). Its distinctive evaluation contribution is benchmarking against human interobserver variability (STAPLE-based semiautomated and pure-manual), showing the model within 5% of human tracers on 8/19 organs and more consistent (lower IQR) than humans on difficult structures. Demonstrates feasibility and failure modes on a pathological RCC population, providing realistic clinical-practice baselines.

ARPM-net is an adversarially trained CNN that combines a multi-residual U-Net variant with multi-scale pooling blocks, an in-network MRF refinement block, and a discriminator operating on elementwise products of CT and label maps, plus a novel adaptive cross-entropy loss that upweights small and low-contrast organs. On 120 pelvic CTs (10-fold CV + 20-case test), it achieved DSC 0.88 (prostate), 0.97 (bladder), 0.86 (rectum), 0.97 (femurs), significantly outperforming residual and multi-residual U-Net baselines on prostate and rectum at ~0.3s per volume. The key novelty is jointly-trained MRF pairwise potentials with adversarial fine-tuning and size/difficulty-adaptive loss weighting in a single network.

This paper proposes SW-DNN, a DeepLabv3+/ResNet101-based segmentation network with a novel stochastic width (SW) mechanism that randomly drops feature maps on four encoder-decoder shortcut connections using linearly decaying survival probabilities, acting as a regularizer and implicit width-ensemble to combat overfitting on small medical datasets. On a newly collected single-center dataset of 150 stomach cancer patients (6,453 CT slices), SW-DeepLabv3+ achieved a mean DSC of 0.7457 (2D) / 0.7530 (3D), statistically significantly outperforming DeepLabv3+, U-Net, and DDCNN for stomach CTV segmentation in radiotherapy planning. The authors claim this is the first automated deep learning approach for stomach cancer CTV contouring, and the SW mechanism is presented as a general-purpose, architecture-agnostic component (also validated on U-Net).

title: Two-stage deep learning model for fully automated pancreas segmentation on computed tomography: Comparison with intra-reader and inter-reader reliability at full and reduced radiation dose on an external dataset
main_contribution: Develops and validates a two-stage 3D U-Net (bounding-box localization followed by volumetric segmentation) trained on the largest pancreas CT cohort reported to date (1917 portal-venous scans), achieving DSC 0.91 internally, 0.89 on NIH-PCT, and 0.84 on external TCIA. Its distinctive contribution is benchmarking the model against intra- and inter-reader reliability, showing the model is MORE stable than radiologists across a 75% radiation-dose reduction (DSC 0.96, CCC 0.995), plus validated generalizability across slice thickness (0.6–3.75 mm) and sex via formal noninferiority testing. Positions the pipeline as a scalable tool for pancreas volumetry and radiomics biomarker discovery, though restricted to morphologically normal pancreases.

title: Automatic delineation of cardiac substructures using a region-based fully convolutional network
organs: ["whole heart", "left atrium", "right atrium", "left ventricle", "right ventricle", "left anterior descending artery (LADA)", "left circumflex (LCFLX)", "left main coronary artery (LMCA)", "right coronary artery (RCA)", "ascending aorta", "pulmonary artery", "superior vena cava", "atrial valve", "mitral valve", "pulmonary valve", "tricuspid valve"]
main_contribution: First adaptation of mask-scoring R-CNN to simultaneous multi-structure cardiac segmentation, delineating the whole heart plus 15 substructures (chambers, great vessels, coronary arteries, valves) on free-breathing radiotherapy CT in a single framework, with a redesigned multilabel RCNN head and an added attention gate as the two key modifications. The mask-scoring head enables probabilistic consolidation of multiple ROI proposals, yielding statistically significant improvements over 3D UNet and Mask R-CNN ablations across DSC, 95% HD, MSD, CMD, and VD (whole heart 0.96; coronaries 0.66 vs 0.48 for UNet), with <5 s inference. The work targets the clinical need for substructure-specific dose-toxicity studies and cardiac-sparing RT planning, though single-institution training (n=45), lack of external validation, and degraded small-structure performance (coronaries/valves) limit current clinical readiness.

title: Interactive contouring through contextual deep learning
architecture: Recurrent Residual U-Net with attention gates (R2U-Net + Attention U-Net)
organs: ["heart", "esophagus", "lung (left)", "lung (right)", "spinal cord", "pancreas", "liver", "submandibular gland (left)", "submandibular gland (right)", "parotid gland (left)", "parotid gland (right)", "brain", "spleen (unseen, test-only)", "lung tumor", "pancreas tumor", "liver tumor", "brain tumor"]
main_contribution: Proposes a semi-automatic 'contextual deep learning' contouring method: an attention-gated R2U-Net takes a target slice plus a previously contoured slice and its mask as a 3-channel input, propagating a single user-drawn contour through a volume without structure-specific class labels. The key finding is that training-set diversity — not structure-specific features — drives generalization: models trained on more structures segment never-seen structures (spleen DSC 0.33→0.80, HD 44→13 mm), enabling de-novo contouring of arbitrary anatomy. Iterative prediction is shown superior to direct propagation for unseen structures.

title: Technical note: Evaluation of a V-Net autosegmentation algorithm for pediatric CT scans: Performance, generalizability, and application to patient-specific CT dosimetry
organs: ["heart", "esophagus", "lung right", "lung left", "small intestine", "large intestine", "spinal canal", "gall bladder", "kidney left", "kidney right", "spleen", "liver", "stomach", "pancreas", "duodenum", "bladder", "rectum", "femoral head right", "femoral head left"]
main_contribution: This technical note provides the first systematic evaluation of 3D FCN (V-Net) autosegmentation on pediatric CT, using a public 359-scan dataset (Pediatric-CT-SEG) across 19 structures, and quantifies generalizability across scanner protocols and patient age — showing models transfer to unseen scanners but not fully across age groups (pancreas), and that combined heterogeneous training matches or beats scanner-/age-specific models. It links segmentation error to clinical consequence via patient-specific CT dose estimation, achieving mean dose error within 5% for 18/19 organs and human-level (interobserver-equivalent) agreement in 13/15 benchmarked structures. The work establishes a reproducible public benchmark and practical deployment pipeline for pediatric organ segmentation in dosimetry.

This paper proposes the Scale Attention Module (SAM), a lightweight channel-style attention that adaptively recalibrates multi-scale features by scoring each scale's importance (GAP+GMP representations fed to a 2-layer MLP), embedded into a HRNet-w18 encoder–neck–decoder network (SANet) for 2D slice-based segmentation of colon, small intestine, and duodenum. Under patient-level five-fold cross-validation on 70 CT scans, SANet achieved 74.18±3.72% mean DSC with a comparable/lower parameter count (10.19M) than UNet, UNet++, AttentionUNet, DeepLabV3p, and CascadedUNet, with its largest gains on the small duodenum (61.68% DSC) and a reported 0.83–2.71 DSC-point advantage over alternative attention and multi-scale feature exploitation strategies. The work demonstrates that efficient exploitation—rather than richer extraction—of multi-scale features can address scale-variability in abdominal OAR segmentation, though validation remains limited to a modest single-center cohort with a 2D approach and no statistical significance testing.

This study provides a controlled, clinically-oriented comparison of four uncertainty quantification approaches (Monte Carlo Dropout, Monte Carlo DropConnect, deep ensembles, and test-time augmentation) built on the same 2D VGG16 U-Net for multi-class kidney/tumor/cyst segmentation on CT. It shows that accuracy is comparable across approaches but uncertainty behavior differs significantly, enabling a risk-propensity-based selection framework: BDR is risk-taking with compact uncertainty regions, while TTA is conservative with large alert regions, and BDR generalizes worst on out-of-distribution data (Qubiq Dice 0.82 vs TTA 0.94). The work also demonstrates current UQ limitations for small, under-represented structures (cysts), where models remain overconfident in wrong predictions.

title: Reinforcement learning-based anatomical maps for pancreas subregion and duct segmentation
architecture: Multiagent RL (DQN) landmark detection + landmark-guided nonrigid registration + U-Net segmentation (3D U-Net, Attention U-Net, Swin U-Netr)
main_contribution: First framework to jointly segment the four pancreatic subregions and the pancreatic duct from 3D CT by coupling multiagent DQN landmark detection with landmark-guided nonrigid atlas registration, whose anatomical probability maps augment standard 3D U-Net variants (3D U-Net, Attention U-Net, Swin U-Netr). Improves mean subregion DSC from 0.38-0.44 (vanilla U-Nets) to 0.47-0.51 and achieves 0.71 duct DSC, with statistical testing and public code/annotations. Clinically significant because even experts disagree on subregion boundaries, which the authors handle transparently via intraobserver agreement baselines.

title: Automatic Segmentation of Pulmonary Lobes Using a Progressive Dense V-Network
main_contribution: PDV-Net combines Dense V-Net feature blocks with progressive holistically nested supervision to segment all five lung lobes end-to-end in a single 3D forward pass (~2 s/CT on a Titan XP), eliminating reliance on prior airway/vessel segmentation, atlases, random-walker post-processing, or user interaction. It achieves Dice 0.939 (LIDC), 0.950 (pathological LTRC), and 0.934 (LOLA11, within 0.004 of the best challenge entry) while being orders of magnitude faster than competing methods. Extensive robustness analyses (vendor, reconstruction kernel, z-spacing, nodule burden, emphysema index) support reliability on both healthy and pathological lungs.

title: PC-U Net: Learning to Jointly Reconstruct and Segment the Cardiac Walls in 3D from CT Data
architecture: PC-U Net: U-Net-style image encoder + PointNet branch + mask decoder
main_contribution: PC-U Net jointly reconstructs a 4096-point 3D point cloud of the LV myocardium wall and its voxel segmentation from 3D CT volumes, using the point cloud as an explicit shape prior fused into a U-Net-style decoder via voxel-wise-multiplied skip connections. Trained end-to-end with Chamfer + soft Dice loss, it matches U-Net Dice (0.885 vs 0.877) while substantially reducing Hausdorff distance (7.05 vs 10.45 mm) on a 20-subject public CT dataset, and yields hole-free 3D surface reconstructions. The work's novelty is the reverse direction as much as the forward one: demonstrating dense masks can be decoded from a sparse point-cloud representation.

title: Self-supervised 3D anatomy segmentation using self-distilled masked image transformer (SMIT)
architecture: Vision Transformer (SWIN-small backbone) with self-supervised self-distillation and masked image modeling
organs: ["spleen", "right kidney", "left kidney", "gallbladder", "esophagus", "liver", "stomach", "aorta", "inferior vena cava", "portal & splenic vein", "pancreas", "adrenal glands", "large bowel (MRI)", "small bowel (MRI)"]
main_contribution: SMIT introduces a self-supervised pre-training scheme for 3D vision transformers combining masked image prediction (dense L1 pixel regression inside masked patches via a 1-layer linear decoder) with masked patch-token and global CLS-token self-distillation from an EMA teacher. Pre-trained on 3,643 heterogeneous CT scans spanning four disease sites, it sets the best reported average Dice on the BTCV 13-organ benchmark (0.878, blinded test) among both supervised transformer baselines and ten SSL pretext tasks, and transfers to MRI abdominal organ segmentation (0.875) without any MRI pre-training data. It further shows reduced fine-tuning data requirements and faster convergence relative to prior medical SSL methods.

title: DeepEdit: Deep Editable Learning for Interactive Segmentation of 3D Medical Images
architecture: U-Net-style CNN / Transformer backbone with click-map input channels (configurable: nnU-Net, UNET, UNETR, SwinUNETR)
organs: ["prostate", "prostatic lesions", "spleen", "liver", "left kidney", "right kidney", "metastatic spines (qualitative only)", "teeth (qualitative only)"]
main_contribution: DeepEdit unifies automatic and click-based interactive 3D segmentation in a single network: Gaussian-smoothed label/background click maps occupy extra input channels, and mixed click-free/simulated-click training enables one model to serve fully automatic, semi-automatic, and refinement modes with multi-label support and pluggable backbones. Against retrained nnU-Net (prostate MRI) and UNETR (BTCV abdominal CT) baselines, simulated clicks substantially improve Dice (prostatic lesion 0.27→0.72 at 10 clicks) while click-free performance stays near automatic-baseline level. Released in MONAI Label with 3D Slicer/OHIF integration, it operationalizes uncertainty-driven active-learning annotation — though with Dice-only evaluation and no real-user or annotation-time validation.

title: Automatic Liver and Lesion Segmentation in CT Using Cascaded Fully Convolutional Neural Networks and 3D Conditional Random Fields
architecture: Cascaded Fully Convolutional Neural Networks (CFCN) based on U-Net
main_contribution: First application of fully convolutional networks to liver CT segmentation via a two-stage cascade of 2D U-Nets, where the first network segments the liver and the second segments lesions within the cropped liver ROI, drastically reducing lesion false positives. A dense 3D conditional random field (mean-field inference) is added as a volumetric post-processing step to enforce spatial coherence across slice-wise 2D predictions, raising liver Dice from 93.1% to 94.3% at <100s per volume. Trained models are open-sourced, and the authors position multi-organ extension via multiple cascaded FCNs as future work.

title: Automated abdominal organ segmentation algorithms for non-enhanced CT for volumetry and 3D radiomics analysis
main_contribution: Two self-configured 3D nnU-Net models segment liver, spleen, and both kidneys on non-enhanced abdominal CT and liver/spleen on low-dose chest CT, achieving external-test DSCs of 0.952-0.969 — matching contrast-enhanced-CT SOTA despite the harder non-contrast input. The main novelty is the downstream reliability analysis rather than the segmentation itself: automated volumetry is trustworthy (ICC >=0.986, <5% error in most cases), and a defined subset of radiomics features (HU statistics, uniformity, entropy, elongation, flatness) is reliably automatable while skewness, kurtosis, and sphericity are not. This enables opportunistic volumetry and fatty-liver assessment from already-acquired non-contrast and low-dose chest CTs, with the model commercialized via MEDIP PRO.

title: Liver Segment and Lesion Segmentation on CT and MRI: An Open-Source Contribution to TotalSegmentator
main_contribution: This study delivers open-source nnU-Net models, contributed to the TotalSegmentator ecosystem, for Couinaud liver segment segmentation on CT (mean Dice 0.897) and MRI (0.847) and a modality-agnostic liver lesion detection/segmentation model trained jointly on CT+MRI (CT: 75.8% sensitivity, Dice 0.658; MRI: 62.7%, 0.337), externally validated zero-shot on LiTS. Its key novelty is a deliberately heterogeneous, generalist multimodal design with Couinaud-level anatomical localization, demonstrated clinically through automated HCC attenuation/volumetry tracking after TACE (median HU 51.33->38.50, p=0.021). The work prioritizes accessibility and broad real-world applicability over peak task-specific performance, candidly documenting the generalizability-specialization trade-off against specialized pipelines such as RetinaNet+U-Net on LiTS.

title: TernaryNet: Faster Deep Model Inference without GPUs for Medical 3D Segmentation using Sparse and Binary Convolutions
main_contribution: First semantic segmentation network to quantise both weights and activations to ternary values {-1,0,+1}, enabled by a novel fully differentiable ternary hyperbolic tangent (ternTanh) trained via tanh-continuation (beta linearly 3->8), replacing floating-point convolutions with masked XOR/XNOR + popcount operations. On NIH pancreas CT (82 scans, 5-fold CV) it is statistically equivalent to its full-precision U-Net (71.0% vs 71.9% Dice, p=0.54) while reducing model memory >15x (0.66 MB) and achieving >10x faster CPU inference, targeting GPU-free clinical and mobile deployment. It also demonstrates that ternary sparsity, not binarisation alone, is the key to avoiding quantisation loss.

title: Double-mix pseudo-label framework: enhancing semi-supervised segmentation on category-imbalanced CT volumes
organs: ["spleen", "right kidney", "left kidney", "gallbladder", "esophagus", "liver", "stomach", "aorta", "IVC", "portal/splenic vein", "pancreas", "right adrenal gland", "left adrenal gland", "left ventricle", "right ventricle", "left atrium", "right atrium", "myocardium", "pulmonary artery", "colon (air/solid regions)"]
main_contribution: Proposes DMPF, a semi-supervised co-training framework on CPS with two differently-initialized 3D V-Nets and EMA teachers, whose Double-Mix pseudo-label module selects categories for mixing augmentation using a novel confidence-difficulty weight (confidence-based information score fused with Dice learning-speed via PSI) plus a voxel-count distribution weight, targeting class-imbalanced CT segmentation. It improves average Dice on difficult categories by +7.0% (BTCV, 40% labeled) and +5.1% (CHD, 5% labeled) over the best of 10 SSL baselines with Wilcoxon significance (p<0.05), and releases code. Main weakness: the mixing module injects noise and underperforms on balanced/simpler datasets.

title: Deep Learning for Automated Liver Segmentation to Aid in the Study of Infectious Diseases in Nonhuman Primates
architecture: Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) with ResNet50 encoder; compared against V-Net and 3D U-Net
main_contribution: This is the first CNN-based automated liver segmentation study in nonhuman primates with viral hemorrhagic fever infections (EBOV, MARV, LASV), addressing a domain with extreme liver size/morphology variability and infection-induced density heterogeneity. It demonstrates that an FPN with a ResNet50 encoder (focal loss, 10-fold subject-wise CV) significantly outperforms V-Net, 3D U-Net (overall Dice 94.08% vs ~92.2%) and an atlas-based baseline (89.0%), while releasing a publicly available dataset of 82 annotated whole-body NHP CTs on Synapse. The work establishes a reproducible baseline for automated organ volumetry to support pathogenesis tracking and medical countermeasure evaluation in preclinical infectious disease research.

title: A Two-Phase Approach using Mask R-CNN and 3D U-Net for High-Accuracy Automatic Segmentation of Pancreas in CT Imaging
main_contribution: The paper proposes a two-phase pancreas segmentation pipeline combining 2D Mask R-CNN (rough localization and cropping) with a custom 3D U-Net (refinement), achieving 86.15% mean DSC on NIH-82 — nominally the best among 16 compared methods — while running on a modest 6 GB consumer GPU. Its main practical contribution is demonstrating that crop-then-segment reduces memory demands enough to make 3D refinement feasible on low-end hardware (~20 s/scan). Ablation confirms both phases contribute, though the margin over prior SOTA (0.16 DSC) is not statistically supported.

title: Robust and smooth Couinaud segmentation via anatomical structure-guided point-voxel network
architecture: Multi-scale point-voxel fusion network (dual-branch: point-based MLP branch + voxel-based 3D CNN branch)
main_contribution: Proposes a multi-scale point-voxel fusion network for automatic Couinaud liver segmentation that embeds vessel-structure attention priors into densely sampled 3D point clouds, fuses point-spatial and voxel-semantic branches via a local attention module, and adds a feature-level distance loss to compact intra-segment features and sharpen uncertain inter-segment boundaries — achieving SOTA Dice (~89–91% in-distribution) on 3Dircadb, LiTS, and MSD8 with demonstrated OOD robustness on thick-slice CT. Secondarily contributes the first publicly released manual Couinaud annotations for 20 3Dircadb and 131 LiTS subjects alongside open code. It is an extended journal version of a prior conference paper.

title: An application of cascaded 3D fully convolutional networks for medical image segmentation
main_contribution: This paper introduces a two-stage coarse-to-fine cascade of multi-class 3D U-Nets for multi-organ and vessel CT segmentation: a first network operating on an automatically generated body-mask candidate region (~40% of voxels) produces dilated foreground predictions (~10% of voxels) that narrow the search space for a second, boundary-focused network. The single shared model — avoiding per-organ models and handcrafted features — achieves state-of-the-art results at the time, including raising external-test pancreas Dice from 68.5 to 82.2% on 150 unseen scans and significantly outperforming 2D FCN baselines on small organs and vessels across 18 structures in 240 scans. Code and trained models are publicly released, making it one of the more reproducible early 3D FCN multi-organ baselines.

title: GLIMS: Attention-Guided Lightweight Multi-Scale Hybrid Network for Volumetric Semantic Segmentation
architecture: Hybrid CNN-Swin Transformer U-shaped volumetric segmentation network (GLIMS)
organs: ["spleen", "right kidney", "left kidney", "gallbladder", "esophagus", "liver", "stomach", "aorta", "inferior vena cava", "portal vein and splenic vein", "pancreas", "right adrenal gland", "left adrenal gland"]
main_contribution: GLIMS is a lightweight hybrid CNN–Swin Transformer U-shaped network for 3D volumetric segmentation that combines depth-wise dilated multi-scale convolution blocks (DACB), a Swin Transformer bottleneck, and attention-guided skip connections (CSAB) with deep supervision. It achieves state-of-the-art mean Dice of 92.14% (BraTS2021) and 84.50% (BTCV multi-organ CT), surpassing nnU-Net and Swin UNETR with fewer parameters (47.16M) and FLOPs (72.30G) than Swin UNETR, at the cost of the slowest inference time among compared models. Within this review's scope, it is a multi-organ CT segmentation method validated only on the 30-scan BTCV benchmark under cross-validation.

title: MSS U-Net: 3D segmentation of kidneys and tumors from CT images with a multi-scale supervised U-Net
main_contribution: The paper presents MSS U-Net, a 6-layer 3D U-Net built on the nnU-Net framework that combines multi-scale deep supervision across decoder layers with exponential logarithmic Soft Dice loss plus weighted cross-entropy, and a connected-component postprocessing rule, to segment kidneys and tumors end-to-end from raw full-scale CT without ROI cropping. It achieves Dice 0.969 (kidney) / 0.805 (tumor) on an internal KiTS19 split and 0.974 / 0.818 on the official KiTS19 challenge test set (7th of 106 teams), demonstrating that training-strategy enhancements to the plain 3D U-Net rival more complex architectures while retaining simplicity and reproducibility. Code is publicly released.

title: OBELISK-Net: Fewer Layers to Solve 3D Multi-Organ Segmentation with Sparse Deformable Convolutions
architecture: OBELISK-Net (sparse deformable 3D convolutions + 1x1 Dense-Net classifier); hybrid OBELISK+CNN variant
organs: ["liver", "spleen", "bladder", "left kidney", "right kidney", "left psoas major muscle", "right psoas major muscle", "pancreas", "stomach", "gallbladder", "duodenum", "esophagus"]
main_contribution: OBELISK-Net replaces stacks of conventional 3D convolutions with a learnable sparse deformable kernel that jointly learns filter coefficients and continuous spatial offsets via differentiable interpolation, followed by a 1x1 Dense-Net classifier, with an optional hybrid combining a shallow U-Net-like CNN for small-organ refinement. Using only ~230k parameters, ~700MB memory, and 87 ms/volume inference, it matches or exceeds parameter-matched and larger U-Net variants on two multi-organ CT benchmarks (82.27% mean Dice on VISCERAL 7 structures; 79.03% mean on TCIA43), demonstrating that deep encoder-decoder stacks are not always necessary when labeled data is scarce. The flexible sparse sampling also enables per-voxel prediction with potential for time-sensitive image-guided interventions.

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Pancreas Segmentation with Multi-atlas Registration and 3D Level-set
architecture: Cascaded coarse-fine-refine pipeline: multi-atlas registration + joint 3D patch-based CNN and 2.5D two-channel U-Nets + 3D distance-regularized level-set (DRLSE)
main_contribution: The paper introduces a fully automated cascaded coarse-fine-refine framework for pancreas CT segmentation that fuses classical and learned components: multi-atlas fast-LDDMM registration for ROI localization, a joint 3D patch-based CNN plus two-channel 2.5D U-Net ensemble (with 3D probability maps fed as a second input channel to capture both local context and global shape), and a 3D distance-regularized level-set refinement with fuzzy-c-means-enhanced edge indicators. Validated on three public datasets with different intensity ranges (ISICDM n=36, NIH n=82, MSD n=281 including tumor cases), it achieves >82% average Dice on all three (84.61% on NIH), surpassing Roth 2015/2016, Zhou 2017, and Cai 2017 under the same 4-fold protocol, and improves worst-case Dice on NIH by ~8 points (70.36%). Its distinctive contribution is explicitly integrating global location, contextual, shape, and edge information - via registration, 3D+2.5D CNNs, and level-sets, respectively - to address the pancreas's small size, shape variability, and ambiguous boundaries.

title: MONAI Label: A framework for AI-assisted Interactive Labeling of 3D Medical Images
architecture: U-Net-based CNNs (DeepGrow, DeepEdit) plus support for arbitrary MONAI Core networks (UNet, HighresNet, DynUNet, ResNet, transformers)
main_contribution: MONAI Label is an open-source (Apache-2.0) client-server framework for AI-assisted interactive 3D medical image annotation, coupling click- and scribble-guided models (DeepGrow, DeepEdit) with active learning and DICOMWeb-based deployment into 3D Slicer and OHIF. On MSD Spleen it reaches Dice 0.967 while reducing annotation time ~10x versus manual contouring. It addresses the annotation bottleneck upstream of segmentation rather than proposing a new segmentation architecture, so its relevance to organ-segmentation accuracy benchmarks is as enabling infrastructure.

title: Cardio-pulmonary substructure segmentation of radiotherapy computed tomography images using convolutional neural networks for clinical outcomes analysis
architecture: DeepLab encoder-decoder with atrous separable convolutions (2D), ResNet-101 backbone
organs: ["heart", "left atrium", "right atrium", "left ventricle", "right ventricle", "aorta", "superior vena cava", "inferior vena cava", "pulmonary artery", "pericardium", "atria", "ventricles"]
main_contribution: A multi-label 2D DeepLab (ResNet-101) system segmenting 12 cardio-pulmonary substructures from contrast and non-contrast thoracic planning CTs, with a loss-function ablation showing cross-entropy outperforms Dice-based losses for long tubular structures (aorta 0.81 to 0.93 DSC). Validation goes beyond geometric overlap to dosimetric equivalence (DVH metrics, p>=0.69) and expert-judged clinical acceptability (85% of contours acceptable without adjustment), cutting contouring time from ~1 h to ~10 s per patient. Models were released via the open-source CERR platform and applied to 283 scans for cardiac toxicity outcomes analysis.

title: A deep learning-based auto-segmentation system for organs-at-risk on whole-body computed tomography images for radiation therapy
architecture: WBNet: anatomic site detection model + three site-specific deep learning segmentation models (Ua-Net, 2.5D U-Net, 3D U-Net)
organs: ["brachial plexus", "brainstem", "constrictor naris", "ears (L/R)", "eyes (L/R)", "hypophysis", "larynx", "lenses (L/R)", "mandible", "optic chiasm", "optic nerves (L/R)", "oral cavity", "parotids (L/R)", "submandibular glands (L/R)", "spinal cord (head/neck, thorax, abdomen)", "sublingual gland", "temporal lobes (L/R)", "thyroid", "temporomandibular joints (L/R)", "trachea (head/neck, thorax)", "esophagus", "heart", "lungs (L/R)", "small bowel", "large bowel", "duodenum", "gallbladder", "kidneys (L/R)", "liver", "pancreas", "spleen", "stomach", "bladder", "femur heads (L/R)", "rectum", "bowel bag"]
main_contribution: This paper presents WBNet, a divide-and-conquer whole-body auto-segmentation system that couples an AlexNet-based anatomic site detector with three site-specific deep segmentation models (Ua-Net for 28 head/neck OARs, 2.5D U-Net for 6 thoracic OARs, patch-based 3D U-Net for 16 abdominal/pelvic OARs), enabling fully automated delineation of 50 OARs across the entire body without manual site or organ selection. Trained/tested on 755 CT scans (505/250 split) with external TCIA validation, it achieved average DSC of 0.84 (in-house) and 0.81 (public) with 6.39 mm/13.71 mm mean 95%HD, outperforming commercial ABAS, AnatomyNet, and nnU-Net on most OARs. Its key clinical contributions are demonstrated delineation time reductions of 61-86% across body sites and clinically acceptable dosimetric agreement in treatment plans of 20 nasopharyngeal cancer patients, establishing practical feasibility for radiation therapy workflows while honestly flagging weaknesses on small/low-contrast and digestive OARs.

title: Convolutional neural network-based automatic liver delineation on contrast-enhanced and non-contrast-enhanced CT images for radiotherapy planning
main_contribution: The key contribution is clinical evidence that a U-Net-like CNN trained exclusively on contrast-enhanced planning CTs (101 cases) generalizes to non-contrast CT (Dice 0.949 vs 0.961 on CECT), with no significant HD difference — the first reported demonstration of this cross-contrast liver transfer, addressing a practical RT-planning gap for contrast-contraindicated patients. The CNN significantly outperformed commercial MIM Maestro auto-segmentation on both Dice and Hausdorff distance (p<0.001) while reducing delineation time from ~10 min to seconds. Its value is as a single-center clinical validation study rather than a methodological advance; the architecture and training details are too under-specified for reproduction or benchmark use.

This prospective, multicenter observational trial (NCT05787522; 500 patients, 5 centers, 37 physicians, 2,483 delineation sets across 11 thoracic OARs) delivers the largest end-user validation to date of deep-learning-assisted OAR auto-segmentation in thoracic radiotherapy, showing that AI-assisted delineation with the commercial 2D U-Net/Res-SE model iCurveE significantly outperforms both manual contouring (vDSC 0.902 vs 0.857; HD95 5.20 vs 8.01 mm; 81.6% contouring-time reduction) and standalone state-of-the-art models (nnU-Net, TotalSegmentator). Beyond accuracy, it uniquely demonstrates that AI assistance narrows inter-center and inter-physician-expertise performance gaps—supporting healthcare equity—characterizes physician–AI interaction dynamics (including attitude effects and longitudinal skill changes), and links improved contouring accuracy to reduced dosimetric (DVH) deviations. For a systematic review on 3D organ segmentation, it is a high-evidence clinical validation study, though its methodology-scoring weakness is the proprietary, non-reproducible model and the fact that the architecture is 2D rather than a fully described 3D network.

title: Active learning for accuracy enhancement of semantic segmentation with CNN-corrected label curations: Evaluation on kidney segmentation in abdominal CT
organs: ["kidney parenchyma (with medulla)", "renal artery", "renal vein", "ureter", "renal cell carcinoma (tumor)"]
main_contribution: Proposes an active-learning framework built on a cascaded 3D U-Net (ROI-localizing U-Net followed by a fine-segmentation U-Net for kidney parenchyma, artery, vein, ureter, and RCC) in which new training labels are produced by manually correcting CNN outputs rather than annotating from scratch. This 'CNN-corrected' labeling halves annotation time (149 to 73 min per case) while average DSC improves monotonically across active-learning stages (54.45 to 71.07) on a small single-center CT dataset. Claims superiority over nnU-Net, but the comparison numbers are not verifiable in the paper and stage-wise gains are not statistically significant.

title: Abdominal multi-organ autosegmentation using 3D-patch-based deep convolutional neural network
main_contribution: This paper presents a 3D-patch-based U-Net (64x64x64 voxel inputs, multi-label output) combined with graph-cut post-processing for auto-segmenting five upper-abdominal organs at risk (liver, stomach, duodenum, bilateral kidneys) on contrast-enhanced 4D-CT from 120 hepatocellular carcinoma patients. The framework significantly outperformed commercial atlas-based autosegmentation on all structures (e.g., liver DSC 0.959 vs 0.808) and was statistically comparable to inter-observer segmentation for liver and kidneys, while reducing segmentation time from 22.6 to 7.1 minutes. Its key significance is clinical validation: it was deployed in routine radiotherapy practice at the authors' institution, an early demonstration of clinically operational DL-based multi-organ autosegmentation for abdominal radiation oncology.

title: Domain-specific cues improve robustness of deep learning-based segmentation of CT volumes
architecture: Stacked CNN ensemble (3D MS-D Nets + 2D nnU-Nets); individually evaluated nnU-Net and MS-D Net
main_contribution: The paper introduces a domain-specific CT preprocessing and augmentation framework (radiologist-oriented HU windowing plus CT-specific augmentation: cluster-wise intensity range shift, slice skipping/interpolation, Gaussian noising, bounded rotation) that plugs into existing CNN pipelines and improves robustness rather than raw accuracy: it matches the Dice of general-purpose multidimensional augmentation while reducing Dice standard deviation by roughly an order of magnitude across samples. Validated architecture-independently on modified nnU-Net and MS-D Net in 2D and 3D on KiTS19 (kidney/tumor) and CHAOS (liver), with a stacked ensemble of 3D MS-D + 2D nnU-Net (top-5 selection per family) achieving the best results (liver 0.980, kidney total 0.947, tumor 0.845). The central message is that encoding radiological workflow priors into data handling - not architecture changes - is the key lever for clinically reliable, low-variance segmentation.

title: Automated pancreas segmentation and volumetry using deep neural network on computed tomography
main_contribution: This study delivers one of the largest-scale clinical validations of deep-learning pancreas segmentation (1,006 abdominal CTs vs. the de facto standard NIH-82), systematically comparing four 3D U-Net variants and identifying the residual dense U-Net as the best performer (DSC 0.842 internal; 0.735 external on NIH TCIA) with clinically reliable volumetry (ICC 0.987 internal). Its principal contributions are large-cohort evidence that segmentation quality and volumetric agreement are achievable on healthy populations, volume-stratified performance analysis, and explicit demonstration of the internal–external generalization gap driven by slice-thickness domain shift. The approach remains semi-automated (manual ROI cropping) and the contribution is validation/methodological rather than a novel architecture.

title: A pipeline for automated deep learning liver segmentation (PADLLS) from contrast enhanced CT exams
architecture: PADLLS: cascade of Dense V-net (Gibson et al.) and H-DenseUnet (Li et al.) with knowledge-based heuristics
main_contribution: This paper introduces PADLLS, a fully automated cascading pipeline that chains a Dense V-net and an H-DenseUNet with knowledge-based heuristics — V-net-derived stomach/spleen mask removal (voxels set to −100 HU), a ROC-optimized 15 HU ascites threshold with morphological filtering, and an extensive post-processing chain — specifically to combat oversegmentation, the dominant failure mode of its constituent networks. On public benchmarks it achieves Dice 0.957 ± 0.033 (SLIVER07) and 0.965 ± 0.016 (3DIRCADb), statistically significantly outperforming both H-DenseUNet and V-net, and reduces ascites-case VOE from 22.99%/51.01% (V-net/H-DenseUNet) to 12.45%. The main trade-offs are high computational cost (~80M parameters, ~64 min/case on an 8GB GPU) and unvalidated performance on pathological livers, but the method is notable for its open-source release (GitHub + Docker) targeting radiomics/radiogenomics workflows.

title: Fully-automated multi-organ segmentation tool applicable to both non-contrast and post-contrast abdominal CT: deep learning algorithm developed using dual-energy CT images
main_contribution: The key contribution is a phase-agnostic 3D nnU-Net multi-organ segmenter (liver, spleen, both kidneys, pancreas) trained efficiently by exploiting DECT: ground-truth masks annotated on portal-venous-phase images are reused on spatiotemporally matched virtual non-contrast images, yielding one algorithm valid on both contrast-enhanced and true non-contrast CT. The architecture feeds predicted internal-organ regions from a body-composition model into nnU-Net to cut inference cost and false positives, and achieves DSC >0.94 for four organs and reliable volumetry (ICC >0.95, >90% within 10% error) across external DECT and cross-vendor SECT test sets — though the pancreas lags (DSC ~0.81–0.87, ~57–73% volumetric accuracy). Main evidence gaps: no code release, no ablation against vanilla nnU-Net, and the dual-input design's claimed efficiency gains are asserted rather than measured.

title: Pancreas segmentation using AI developed on the largest CT dataset with multi-institutional validation and implications for early cancer detection
main_contribution: Trains a 3D nnU-Net v2 ensemble on the largest single-institution pancreas CT dataset to date (n=3031, radiologist-annotated) and achieves state-of-the-art fully automated pancreas segmentation (DSC 0.94 internal, 0.96 on curated AbdomenCT-1K external set with newly created expert ground truth to be released publicly, significantly outperforming TotalSegmentator). Key contributions are scale, rigorous multi-dataset external validation including clinically oriented volume-agreement analysis (CCC, Bland-Altman), a novel expert-annotated external ground-truth resource, and a systematic failure-mode analysis. The contribution is dataset- and validation-driven rather than architectural novelty; no code or model weights are released.

title: Deformable multi-head cross attention-based 3D U-net for context-aware multi-modal cardiac image segmentation with uncertainty-aware maps
architecture: 3D U-Net + Swin Transformer + deformable Multi-Head Cross-Attention (MHCA)
main_contribution: Proposes a multimodal 3D cardiac segmentation framework combining a 3D U-Net backbone, Swin Transformer context encoding, and a novel deformable multi-head cross-attention (learnable 3D voxel offsets, K=4 samples/head) for CT/MRI feature fusion, unified with MC-Dropout + heteroscedastic uncertainty maps and DeepSHAP explainability. Achieves Dice 91.8% (MSD-LA), 92.3% (ACDC), 93.2% (MMWHS), with paired t-test significance over U-Net and Swin baselines, at the cost of ~190 ms inference and 8.5 GB GPU memory. Main gap relative to clinical review standards: no per-organ reporting, no external validation, and no released code.

title: Submanifold Sparse Convolutional Networks for Automated 3D Segmentation of Kidneys and Kidney Tumours in Computed Tomography
architecture: 3D Submanifold Sparse Convolutional U-Net (SSCN), two-stage pipeline
main_contribution: This paper reports the first application of submanifold sparse convolutional networks (SSCNs) to 3D CT organ/tumour segmentation, combining Hounsfield-unit-based voxel sparsification with a two-stage sparse U-Net pipeline (low-resolution ROI detection followed by high-resolution segmentation within cropped components). On KiTS23 (5-fold CV), it achieves accuracy competitive with retrained nnU-Net and top KiTS23 challenge teams (Dice 95.8% kidneys+masses, 85.7% tumour+cyst, 80.3% tumour) while reducing inference time by up to 60% and VRAM by up to 75% versus an architecture-matched dense U-Net, enabling full-resolution native 3D inference on 16 GB GPUs. The principal contribution is a resource-efficiency-oriented methodology demonstrating sparse convolutions as a viable alternative to dense/patch-based pipelines in medical imaging, rather than a new state-of-the-art in accuracy.

title: DRAN: Deep recurrent adversarial network for automated pancreas segmentation
architecture: DRAN: deep recurrent adversarial network (segmentation network as generator + discriminative network)
main_contribution: This paper proposes DRAN, an end-to-end adversarial framework combining (i) a dilated convolution autoencoder with adaptive dilated blocks for resolution-preserving multi-scale context, (ii) a novel Local-LSTM module operating on patches serialized via a Hilbert space-filling curve to model intra-slice spatial context for boundary refinement, and (iii) a discriminator with hybrid BCE+perceptual loss and Laplacian-smoothed DSC loss to enforce inter-slice smoothness. It achieves state-of-the-art pancreas segmentation on the standard 80-volume NIH benchmark (DSC 89.87±3.17% via 4-fold CV), outperforming U-Net/FCN/SegNet/DeepLab v3+ and prior pancreas-specific methods, with a parameter-efficient design (103M parameters). For the systematic review, this represents a medium-quality single-organ, effectively-2D methodological contribution notable for its GAN-LSTM hybrid design but lacking external validation, code release, and inferential statistical analysis.

title: Interactive 3D U-net for the segmentation of the pancreas in computed tomography scans
main_contribution: This paper introduces iUnet, an interactive 3D U-Net in which only the final layer and one deep latent layer are per-case fine-tuned on user scribbles via a weighted soft-Dice loss with a volume-penalty term, removing the organ-specific post-processing that the earlier iFCN interactive framework required and that fails for the pancreas. iUnet achieved a stronger automatic baseline than iFCN and the canonical Çiçek 3D U-Net (78.1% vs 72.3% and 75.3% DSC, 5-fold CV on 90 public CTs), and in a three-observer study on an external 10-scan Radboud UMC cohort reached near-interobserver-expert accuracy (86.0% DSC) in a median 8 minutes versus 15 minutes for manual segmentation (48.4% time reduction, p<0.001). Its key contribution is demonstrating that scribble-based interactive deep-learning refinement can attain expert-level pancreas segmentation roughly twice as fast as manual annotation, with a design the authors claim is organ- and modality-agnostic.

title: Pancreas Segmentation with Probabilistic Map Guided Bi-directional Recurrent UNet
architecture: PBR-UNet: probabilistic-map-guided bi-directional recurrent 2.5D UNet (two-stage: M-FCN initial estimation + 2.5D UNet primary segmentation)
main_contribution: This paper proposes PBR-UNet, a two-stage 2.5D framework in which multi-view FCN probabilistic maps are combined with the center-slice image into a local 3D hybrid multi-channel input, which is iteratively refined by a novel bi-directional recurrent update scheme inside a 2.5D UNet — balancing 2D efficiency against 3D context exploitation. Achieving 85.35±4.13% DSC on NIH (4-fold CV) and 85.65% on MSD with only 75M parameters (~0.57 s/slice), it matches or exceeds heavier 3D competitors while particularly improving poorly-segmented, small-target slices. The bi-directional recurrent guidance paradigm is presented as a plug-in alternative to costly 3D convolutions for context modeling in medical image segmentation.

Presents a custom CNN for whole-heart segmentation from cardiac CT aimed at speeding up 3D surgical planning models, achieving IoU 0.85 and reducing segmentation time from a reported ~30 h manual median to 5 min automated (+ up to 3 h human correction). Contribution is primarily a workflow/feasibility demonstration on 2 HOCM cases rather than a methodological advance; no architecture, loss, or comparative evaluation details are provided, so it serves as a low-evidence clinical-translation data point in this review.

title: Accurate fully automated assessment of left ventricle, left atrium, and left atrial appendage function from computed tomography using deep learning
architecture: nnU-Net (best performer), compared against 3D TransUNet and UNETR
organs: ["left ventricle", "left atrium", "left atrial appendage", "ascending aorta", "pulmonary veins"]
main_contribution: First study to show that stroke volume and ejection fraction of the LV, LA, and LAA can be simultaneously estimated from time-resolved CT using fully automatic 3D deep learning. nnU-Net outperformed two ViT-based architectures (mean DSS 0.91 vs 0.89 for 3D TransUNet vs 0.69 for UNETR) and was the only method to reliably predict LAA ejection fraction (ICC 0.68), supporting the conclusion that convolutional encoders with multi-scale skip connections remain superior to transformer encoders for this task, while 3D TransUNet offers ~7× faster inference (41 s vs 276 s/volume).

title: A slice classification model-facilitated 3D encoder–decoder network for segmenting organs at risk in head and neck cancer
architecture: Two-step model: slice classification CNN + refined 3D encoder–decoder segmentation network
organs: ["brainstem", "right eye", "left eye", "right optic nerve", "left optic nerve", "right temporal lobe", "left temporal lobe", "right parotid", "left parotid", "right temporomandibular joint", "left temporomandibular joint", "mandible"]
main_contribution: The paper proposes a two-step pipeline for H&N OAR auto-segmentation in which a lightweight slice classifier (six craniocaudal categories, 95.99% accuracy) first excludes irrelevant slices (~71% on average) before a refined 3D dilated encoder-decoder with SELU activations and inter-stack skip concatenations segments each of 12 OARs. This class-imbalance-targeting design cuts false positives on irrelevant slices and reduces total inference time by 21.16% (40.13 s vs 50.90 s) while significantly improving DSC for 8/12 OARs and 95HD for 11/12 versus the same network without the classifier. Its main limitation is the per-OAR independent network design, which ignores inter-organ spatial context and yields 12 separate models requiring retraining per organ.

title: nnU-Net Deep Learning Method for Segmenting Parenchyma and Determining Liver Volume From Computed Tomography Images
main_contribution: Demonstrates that the self-configuring nnU-Net (3D U-Net, ~19M parameters) achieves near-radiologist liver segmentation (Dice 0.974, HD95 2.46 mm) and clinically actionable volume estimation (1.92% mean error) on an external 20-scan IRCAD test set, exceeding published Dice of liver-specialist architectures (H-DenseUNet 0.965, RA-UNet 0.961) without task-specific tuning. The translational contribution is the complete segmentation-to-volume-to-3D-rendering pipeline aimed at pre-transplant donor/recipient size matching, with high per-case consistency (Dice SD 0.005). Credibility is limited by the single-organ scope, small external test set, absence of released code, and test-set monitoring during training.

title: Deep Learning Initialized and Gradient Enhanced Level-set Based Segmentation for Liver Tumor from CT Images
architecture: Coarse-to-fine cascade: 2D U-Net -> 3D FCN -> DRLSE level-set with FCM-enhanced edge indicator
main_contribution: This paper proposes a hybrid data-driven/model-driven pipeline for liver and liver tumor CT segmentation: a 2D U-Net and 3D FCN cascade performs coarse-to-fine liver segmentation while automatically initializing a distance-regularized level-set evolution (DRLSE), whose edge indicator is enhanced by unsupervised fuzzy c-means probability maps combined via a max operation with image gradients. The key novelties are eliminating the manual ROI requirement of level-set methods and FCM-based edge enhancement, yielding competitive results on two public benchmarks (liver Dice 96.3-96.7%; tumor Dice 71.8% per-case/84.1% global on LiTS, comparable to H-DenseUNet) at ~90 s/volume. The work demonstrates that coupling CNN initialization with level-set refinement improves tumor boundary accuracy, stability (reduced variance), and topology interpretability relative to pure deep learning baselines.

title: Prior Attention Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network Based Automatic Segmentation of Organs at Risk for Head and Neck Cancer Radiotherapy
architecture: PANet (Prior Attention enhanced CNN) within a Stepwise Refinement Segmentation Framework (SRSF)
organs: ["brainstem", "spinal cord", "optic chiasm", "pituitary", "temporal lobes (L/R)", "eyes (L/R)", "optic nerves (L/R)", "lens (L/R)", "middle ears (L/R)", "mastoids (L/R)", "mandibles (L/R)", "temporomandibular joints (L/R)", "parotids (L/R)"]
main_contribution: The paper proposes PANet, a pyramidal U-Net variant combining justified inception blocks with a prior attention + learnable spatial attention (PAI) block, embedded in a three-stage Stepwise Refinement Segmentation Framework (OGS -> LOS -> SOS) that segments 22 head-and-neck OARs coarse-to-fine on full-resolution CT. Prior probability maps from earlier stages serve both ROI localization and attention guidance, addressing the large/small organ imbalance without per-organ models. It achieves the best reported small-OAR Dice on MICCAI 2015 (77.6% left optic nerve, 69.2% chiasm) with ~30s inference, though it underperforms baselines on chiasm/pituitary and training requires complex 5-fold cross-validated prior-map generation.

title: Automatic Liver Segmentation Using Multi-plane Integrated Fully Convolutional Neural Networks
architecture: MPNet: multi-plane integrated fully convolutional network
main_contribution: Proposes MPNet, a pseudo-3D factorized-convolution FCN (3x3x1 intra-slice + 1x1x3 inter-slice kernels) with residual connections, dilated convolutions, encoder-decoder skips, and multi-scale prediction fusion, trained independently in axial, coronal, and sagittal planes and combined by averaging softmax outputs at test time. Achieves 96.7% mean Dice on LiTS 2017 liver segmentation using a single framework with no pre/post-processing beyond 1mm^3 resampling, matching the top leaderboard entry while avoiding the coarse-to-fine pipelines and refinement stages used by competitors. The main empirical evidence is the ablation showing multi-plane integration lifts Dice from 0.685 (axial-only) to 0.967, largely by rescuing low-slice-count volumes where the axial model fails.

title: CC-DenseUNet: Densely Connected U-Net with Criss-Cross Attention for Liver and Tumor Segmentation in CT Volumes
architecture: CC-DenseUNet: densely connected U-Net (DenseNet-121 backbone) with criss-cross attention (CCA) module at the bottleneck
main_contribution: CC-DenseUNet inserts a criss-cross attention module (from CCNet) into the bottleneck of a DenseNet-121-based densely connected U-Net, processing CT volumes in 2.5D (three adjacent slices) with ImageNet transfer learning. On a custom 100/31 LiTS split it reports liver/tumor Dice of 0.962/0.741 and on 3DIRCADb 2-fold CV 0.943/0.663, edging out H-DenseUNet on tumor Dice by 1-2% while staying competitive on liver. The clinical relevance for multi-organ review is limited: single-organ (liver+tumor) scope, non-benchmark split, no significance testing, and the tumor Dice gain is within plausible run-to-run variance.

title: Automatic liver segmentation on CT images combining region-based techniques and convolutional features
architecture: 3D U-Net fused with traditional region-based pipeline (region growing + Chan-Vese active contour + PDF thresholding + GrowCut)
main_contribution: Proposes a hybrid fusion of a training-free traditional pipeline (PDF-based thresholding, Chan-Vese active contour, multi-axis 2D region growing) with a 3D U-Net prediction mask refined by anatomical constraints and GrowCut, weighted 0.5/0.5, plus a fast lung-based liver-heart separation step. The main claim is robustness under data scarcity: fusion remains stable across heterogeneous scanners (DSC 0.89-0.91) where the U-Net alone collapses on unseen data (DSC 0.79-0.81), though the U-Net alone wins when sufficient training data exists. Evaluated on SLIVER, VISCERAL, and a small private DB with 10 overlap/surface metrics; results are comparable to SOTA on SLIVER but with notably large maximum surface distances.

title: Medical Images Sequence Normalization and Augmentation: Improve Liver Tumor Segmentation From Small Dataset
main_contribution: This paper proposes a comprehensive data preprocessing and augmentation pipeline for liver and liver tumor segmentation from small CT datasets, combining intensity normalization with custom thresholding, 2D geometric augmentation, slice interpolation, and novel organ-centered 3D augmentation. Using a two-phase cascaded FCN (CFCN) with dense CRF on 3D-IRCADb-01, the pipeline improves liver Dice from 91.47% to 94.58% and tumor Dice from 27.17% to 45.87%. The key novelty is the 3D augmentation strategy that uses the organ's central point as the transformation origin to maximize preserved organ area while generating multi-perspective training samples from oblique slices.

title: Automatic Pulmonary Vein and Left Atrium Segmentation for TAPVC Preoperative Evaluation Using V-Net with Grouped Attention
main_contribution: Proposes GAB-V-Net, a modified V-Net (residuals removed, Instance Norm, and a novel Grouped Attention Block combining K=4 CBAM-inspired spatial-and-channel attention blocks with grouped convolution) for the first automatic segmentation (per authors) of pulmonary veins and left atrium in low-dose CT of pediatric TAPVC patients. On 68 single-center scans with 5-fold CV, it reaches DSC 0.795 (PV) and 0.834 (LA), outperforming V-Net and 3D-UNet with fully automatic pre/post-processing and ~400 ms inference versus 2–3 hours of manual delineation. Clinical claim: enables faster preoperative evaluation and surgical planning for TAPVC while reducing radiologist workload.

title: 3D Segment and Pickup Framework for Pancreas Segmentation
architecture: LS-ResNet (long and short residual network): 3D U-Net-style encoder-decoder, used within the proposed Segment and Pickup (SAP) framework with two networks (SeedNet and SegNet)
main_contribution: This paper proposes the Segment-and-Pickup (SAP) framework as an alternative to coarse-to-fine locate-and-segment pipelines for pancreas CT segmentation: at training time a ground-truth-derived Euclidean-distance contour ROI (d=16) trains a high-precision SegNet free of class imbalance, while at test time a whole-scan SeedNet supplies a clean seed for region-growing pickup of correct components from SegNet's noisy output. Combined with LS-ResNet, a 3D U-Net variant with long- and short-range residual shortcuts, it achieves 86.96% DSC (Jaccard 74.62%) on the NIH pancreas dataset (82 scans, 4-fold CV), surpassing their matched C2F baseline (86.25%) and most compared methods, though trailing Li et al. (87.57%). The contribution is primarily a framework/training-strategy insight (oracle contour ROI + seed-based noise rejection) rather than a novel architecture.

title: A Simple and Robust Framework for Cross-Modality Medical Image Segmentation applied to Vision Transformers
architecture: Conditional Vision Transformer (C-ViT) encoder with U-Net style decoder (applied to Swin-UNETR); conditional 3D residual U-Net
organs: ["whole heart (WH)", "left ventricle blood cavity (LV)", "right ventricle blood cavity (RV)", "left atrium blood cavity (LA)", "right atrium blood cavity (RA)", "left ventricle myocardium (MYO)", "ascending aorta (AA)", "pulmonary artery (PA)"]
main_contribution: This paper proposes a general cross-modality segmentation framework that conditions encoder normalization layers via modality-switched Conditional Instance Normalization (CIN), trained end-to-end with non-registered, interleaved mixed MRI+CT data — eliminating the need for registered image pairs, GAN-based synthetic translation, or dual-stream architectures. Building on it, the authors introduce the Conditional Vision Transformer (C-ViT) encoder (LN replaced by CIN in transformer blocks, applied to Swin-UNETR), which improves whole-heart Dice by up to 6.87% over its baseline and relaxes the data-hunger typical of ViTs. On MM-WHS 2017 with CT as target, the conditional 3D UNet variant achieves state-of-the-art cross-modality performance (90.77% mean Dice), outperforming fine-tuning, joint training, X-shaped architectures, GAN translation, and mutual knowledge distillation, while retaining high-quality bidirectional (MRI) segmentation.

title: Hybrid 3D-ResNet Deep Learning Model for Automatic Segmentation of Thoracic Organs at Risk in CT Images
architecture: 3D ResNet-based encoder-decoder U-Net with Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) and Project & Excite (PE) modules
main_contribution: Proposes a hybrid 3D ResNet encoder-decoder U-Net with a 3D-adapted ASPP module at the bottleneck and Project & Excite (PE) recalibration blocks at every encoder/decoder stage, applied to multiclass segmentation of four thoracic organs at risk (heart, aorta, trachea, esophagus) on SegTHOR 2019. The contribution is an incremental combination of existing modules (ResNet, ASPP, PE), reported to achieve Dice 98.53 / HD 0.24 mm without post-processing, outperforming eight published SegTHOR methods. Validity is weak: no loss function or code, aggregate-only results, and reported scores implausibly exceed all published SegTHOR benchmarks.

Applies a hybrid 2D+3D densely-connected UNet (with ResNet-based liver localization) to liver and tumor CT segmentation, motivated by surgical planning workflows, reporting a 96.2% global Dice on 35 mixed public/private test scans. The architecture closely mirrors prior H-DenseUNet work, and the contribution is best characterized as a surgical-context application with preprocessing/postprocessing refinements rather than a methodological advance. Evaluation is limited to a single aggregate metric with no statistical analysis, per-structure results, or quantitative SOTA comparison, limiting evidential weight for the reported performance.

title: Automatic Segmentation of Kidney and Renal Tumor in CT Images Based on 3D Fully Convolutional Neural Network with Pyramid Pooling Module
architecture: 3D_FCN_PPM (3D Fully Convolutional Network with Pyramid Pooling Module)
main_contribution: This paper introduces 3D_FCN_PPM, an end-to-end 3D fully convolutional network combining ResNet residual blocks, reduced pooling, dilated convolutions, and a 4-branch pyramid pooling module for joint kidney and renal tumor segmentation in arterial-phase CT angiography — reportedly the first 3D deep learning attempt for this combined task. Evaluated on 140 single-center patients (90 train / 50 test), it achieved Dice coefficients of 0.931 (kidney) and 0.802 (tumor), outperforming retrained 2D PSPNet and 3D UNet baselines on identical data, with 3D contextual information shown to be critical for discriminating tumors from adjacent tissue. Key open issues are under-segmentation of small tumors (<~10ml), prediction bias near the renal hilum, dependence on a prior multi-atlas ROI localization step, and no code or external validation.

title: SequentialSegNet: Combination with Sequential Feature for Multi-organ Segmentation
architecture: SequentialSegNet (SSN): U-Net-style FCN with bi-directional ConvLSTM sequential feature extractors on skip connections
main_contribution: SequentialSegNet augments a U-Net-style multi-class FCN with bi-directional ConvLSTM 'sequential feature extractors' on the upper skip connections, capturing inter-slice context from 7-slice chunks while avoiding the memory and training cost of 3D convolutions. On LiTS (plus self-annotated spleen/gallbladder masks verified by a radiologist), it outperforms a multi-organ 2D U-net on all three organs under 4-fold CV (liver 95.91, spleen 91.30, gallbladder 75.57 Dice) with roughly half the inference time of a hierarchical 3D FCN. Its most distinctive contribution is a failure-mode analysis of gallbladder extirpation (~16% of cases), an under-reported scenario in prior multi-organ work, showing the recurrent model yields fewer false positives (FP ratio 80.95% vs 90.48%).

title: Segmentation of Organs at Risk in Thoracic CT Images Using a SharpMask Architecture and Conditional Random Fields
architecture: FCN with SharpMask feature-fusion refinement + CRF as RNN (CRFasRNN)
main_contribution: This paper presents one of the first deep learning frameworks for joint segmentation of four thoracic organs at risk (esophagus, heart, trachea, aorta), combining an FCN with SharpMask-style top-down feature fusion and an end-to-end trainable CRFasRNN module that learns spatial relationships between neighboring organs. The SharpMask fusion yields statistically significant gains over plain FCN (p<0.05 for 3/4 organs) and outperforms OPAL label fusion on esophagus, heart, and aorta, while the learned CRF compatibility adds flexibility over the Potts model — though CRF gains themselves are largely non-significant. The work establishes an early baseline for joint thoracic OAR delineation, notable for honest negative results, but is constrained by a 30-scan private dataset, Dice-only evaluation, and unclear 2D vs 3D convolution dimensionality.

Proposes the Multi-scale Prediction Network (MPN): a filter-reduced U-Net with residual blocks that emits five prediction maps at multiple scales, all supervised by Dice loss during training and averaged at inference. On 130 lesion-enriched thoracic CTs (LUNA16+NLST) with radiologist-corrected ground truth, MPN yields marginal gains in Dice (0.9845 vs. 0.9830 baseline) but notable gains in Hausdorff distance and nodule-area coverage (87.54% vs. 52.26% for 3D V-Net). Its main conceptual contribution is demonstrating that mean Dice hides failures on pleura-attached nodules, motivating region-specific coverage metrics for segmentation evaluation.

title: Learning to Segment the Lung Volume from CT Scans Based on Semi-Automatic Ground-Truth
main_contribution: The paper demonstrates that a 3D CNN can be trained on noisy, semi-automatically generated lung labels (LUNA16) and still achieve expert-grade segmentation on externally validated data (VESSEL12: 98.7% Dice, 0.576mm ASD), outperforming standard V-Net especially at lung boundaries. Architecturally, it introduces an early max-pooling layer plus an input-to-output skip connection that lets V-Net ingest full-resolution 512x512x256 CT volumes without downsampling or patching. Its main value to this review is as evidence that pseudo-labels can substitute for costly manual 3D annotation, though it is limited to a single organ and lacks statistical rigor.

title: Automated Segmentation of Pulmonary Lobes Using Coordination-Guided Deep Neural Networks
organs: ["pulmonary lobes (right upper, right middle, right lower, left upper, left lower lung lobes)"]
main_contribution: This paper proposes an end-to-end 3D pulmonary lobe segmentation network based on V-net, enhanced with 3D CoordConv layers that inject normalized positional coordinates at the final decoding stage to resolve inter-lobe misclassification, combined with U-Net-based lung ROI preprocessing, group normalization, and an auxiliary fissure/boundary Dice loss. Evaluated by five-fold cross-validation on 343 chest CTs from four sources (LUNA16, LKDS, Meinian, LOLA11), it achieves a state-of-the-art mean Dice of 0.947±0.044 versus 0.926 for the best prior method (FR-vnet), with ~12 s processing per case. The main insight—that explicit positional encoding plus boundary-aware auxiliary supervision substantially improves lobe segmentation—is convincingly demonstrated via ablations, though validation is limited to internal cross-validation without external testing, statistical significance testing, or code release.

title: An Efficient Hybrid Model for Kidney Tumor Segmentation in CT Images
architecture: HybridNet: V-Net (foreground) + Submanifold Sparse Convolutional Network on point clouds (fine-grained segmentation)
main_contribution: HybridNet is a two-stage model combining a V-Net foreground segmenter with a Submanifold Sparse Convolutional Network (SSCN) that operates on a voxel-to-point-cloud representation of the foreground, enabling whole-ROI context learning, native handling of CT anisotropy via z-axis stretching, and ~9x lower training GPU memory than full-ROI patch-based 3D FCN baselines. It achieves 84.9 (validation) / 79.7 (official test) tumor Dice on KiTS19 with only 2.7M parameters and 0.22 s/sample, and a coordinates-only ablation shows superior geometric robustness versus conventional voxel CNNs. Its main novelty is being the first hybrid voxel + point-cloud pipeline for 3D medical segmentation, though evaluation is limited to a single dataset with tumor-only reporting.

title: A Triple-Stage Self-Guided Network for Kidney Tumor Segmentation
main_contribution: Proposes a triple-stage coarse-to-fine self-guided cascade (low-resolution localization net -> full-resolution segmentation net -> tumor refine net) in which each stage consumes the previous stage's prediction as guidance, motivated by nnU-Net. Two technical novelties: dilated convolution blocks replacing deep-layer pooling to retain small-tumor detail, and a dynamic hybrid loss (dice + distance-map-weighted cross-entropy + hard-example dice on the previous stage's error voxels). Achieved 2nd place in KiTS19 with kidney/tumor/composite Dice of 0.9674/0.8454/0.9064, with ablations attributing ~0.8-1.6 Dice points to each component.

title: Liver Segmentation in CT with MRI Data: Zero-Shot Domain Adaptation by Contour Extraction and Shape Priors
architecture: 3D U-Net (Çiçek et al.) with edge enhancement module and convolutional autoencoder shape-prior regularization
main_contribution: The paper proposes a zero-shot MRI→CT domain adaptation strategy for 3D liver segmentation that requires no target-domain data, combining (a) fixed 3D Sobel-kernel edge enhancement to bias the network toward modality-invariant contour/shape features and (b) an autoencoder-derived latent shape-prior regularization added to the Dice loss. Ablations show edge enhancement is the dominant factor, and the combined model improves vanilla 3D U-Net from 44.6% to 69.2% average DSC across three independent CT cohorts, approaching supervised fine-tuning on TCIA (81.7% vs 82.8%) without seeing any CT during training. It is the first application of contour- and shape-based regularization to zero-shot cross-modality medical segmentation, though results are single-organ and clearly below supervised fine-tuning.

title: Deep Learning and Unsupervised Fuzzy C-Means Based Level-Set Segmentation for Liver Tumor
main_contribution: Proposes a fully automatic coarse-to-fine liver tumor segmentation pipeline in which a cascaded 2D U-Net + 3D FCN localizes and refines the liver and roughly localizes the tumor, and a distance-regularized level-set refines tumor contours. The key novelty is an enhanced edge indicator gmax = max(gi, gp) fusing image gradients with an unsupervised fuzzy c-means probability map, combined with automatic contour initialization from the eroded FCN output — removing the manual ROI initialization required by prior level-set methods. The level-set refinement raises mean tumor DSC from 66.76% to 72.45% (3-fold CV, +5.69%) with the largest gains on challenging cases (min DSC 27.85% -> 40.04%), and achieves 74.26% on the hidden challenge test set.

title: Structure Correction for Robust Volume Segmentation in Presence of Tumors
architecture: Multi-stage pipeline: V-Net (Stage 1) + 3D structure correction CNN (Stage 2) + flood-fill refinement (Stage 3)
main_contribution: A three-stage lung segmentation pipeline (V-Net → 3D structure-correction CNN → parallel flood-fill) in which the correction stage is trained exclusively on synthetically corrupted masks from normal lungs, eliminating the need for pathological ground-truth annotations. It recovers at least 15% more juxtapleural tumor voxels than CNN state-of-the-art while maintaining accuracy on normal lungs, and runs in ~2.7s per CT versus 189-586s for classical shape-prior methods. The core novelty is the corruption-based augmentation that injects lung shape prior without requiring tumor-segmented training data.

title: Bridging the Gap between 2D and 3D Contexts in CT Volume for Liver and Tumor Segmentation
architecture: Full-context CNN combining 2D Spatial-Net and 3D Temporal-Net with squeeze-and-excitation (SE) fusion layer
main_contribution: Proposes a 'full-context' CNN that jointly learns 2D intra-slice context (Spatial-Net with dense connections) and 3D inter-slice context (Temporal-Net), fused through a squeeze-and-excitation layer to bridge the trade-off between preserving in-plane spatial detail and exploiting volumetric temporal information in CT. This is complemented by a ground-truth-informed overlapped slice-based input scheme and a weighted cross-entropy + Jaccard distance loss to counter extreme class imbalance. Achieves competitive liver segmentation (DSC 0.968 LiTS test; 0.965 3D-IRCADB) and tumor segmentation (DSC up to 0.824 LiTS test) against 12 prior methods, though tumor Dice remains markedly lower than liver Dice and no code is released.

title: U-Net and Mean-Shift Histogram for Efficient Liver Segmentation from CT Images
main_contribution: This paper presents a fast liver segmentation pipeline combining a 2D U-Net with two lightweight plug-in components: a CDF-based image enhancement (NCDF) that suppresses unlikely regions during preprocessing, and a mean-shift clustering over per-axis projection histograms that adds compact 3D context post-hoc to remove over-segmentation. On SLIVER07 via 5-fold cross-validation, the full configuration achieves a median Dice of 0.95 at ~38 s per CT volume, deliberately trading modest accuracy against slower prior methods (~9.5x speed advantage) for time-sensitive clinical workflows.

This paper proposes DD-UNet++, a modified U-Net++ that replaces standard convolutions with dilated convolutions (rates 1, 2, 4, 8) in the innermost and penultimate layers to enlarge the receptive field and capture global pelvic context without added depth or resolution loss. On a private single-center dataset of ~11,000 CT slices from 62 post-hysterectomy acquisitions, DD-UNet++ modestly outperforms standard U-Net++ in 10-fold cross-validated Dice scores for bladder (93.2% vs 91.2%), CTV (89% vs 85%), and rectum (87.6% vs 84.7%) at negligible additional training cost (+6s/iteration). The authors claim it is the first application of U-Net++ to CTV and OAR segmentation in post-hysterectomy pelvic CT.

title: Reliable automatic organ segmentation from CT images using deep CNN
main_contribution: The paper presents a residual-learning-enhanced 3D U-Net combined with a novel four-channel input preprocessing scheme (original CT, two adaptive histogram equalizations with different tile sizes, and a Laplacian edge map) for automatic bladder and rectum segmentation in pelvic CT for radiotherapy planning. On a private 66-patient single-center dataset it achieves mean DSC of 91.2% (bladder) and 81.8% (rectum), marginally outperforming V-Net and two 2015 regression-based methods on bladder at the cost of slower inference (2.1 s vs 0.9 s). The contribution is incremental-combining established components (3D U-Net, residual connections, contrast enhancement)-and the evidence is substantially limited by the small dataset, undefined train/test protocol, absent statistical analysis, and no external validation.

title: Automatic Multi-organ Segmentation on Abdominal CT with Dense V-networks
architecture: DenseVNet (Dense V-network, fully convolutional neural network)
main_contribution: This paper introduces DenseVNet, a memory-efficient 3D fully convolutional network combining DenseNet-style dense feature stacks, a shallow multi-scale V-structure, batch-wise spatial dropout, dilated convolutions, and a trainable low-resolution spatial prior, for registration-free segmentation of eight abdominal organs (pancreas, esophagus, stomach, duodenum, liver, spleen, gallbladder, left kidney) from CT. In 9-fold cross-validation on 90 multi-centre scans, it achieved significantly higher Dice than VNet, VoxResNet, and the DEEDS+JLF multi-atlas method for all organs (e.g., pancreas 0.78 vs 0.71-0.74; esophagus 0.76 vs 0.66-0.69; duodenum 0.63 vs 0.56-0.60), with the largest gains on small organs. Ablation studies established dense connectivity and multi-scale structure as the critical accuracy drivers, while showing dilated convolutions, spatial prior, hinge loss, and Monte Carlo inference can be omitted without significant performance loss.

title: Two-Stage Multi-Organ Automatic Segmentation with Low GPU Memory Occupancy
organs: ["liver", "spleen", "pancreas", "right kidney", "left kidney", "stomach", "gallbladder", "esophagus", "aorta", "inferior vena cava", "right adrenal gland", "left adrenal gland", "duodenum"]
main_contribution: Proposes a two-stage coarse-to-fine framework (Tiny-CED Net, a 1.328M-parameter lightweight 3D U-Net variant) that segments 13 abdominal organs from whole CT volumes using <2GB GPU memory and <25s inference, targeting labs without high-end GPUs. On a 40/10 split of FLARE22 it reaches 0.83 average DSC, slightly beating a much larger 3D U-Net baseline (0.81) on DSC and ASSD, at the cost of higher surface distance deviation (SSD) and persistently weak small-organ accuracy (duodenum, adrenal glands). Main novelty is the low-memory coarse-localize-then-fine-segment trade-off rather than architectural innovation.

The paper presents RayPlus, a web-based (B/S) platform delivering liver surgery planning tools — semi-automatic liver/vessel/tumor segmentation, Hessian-filter vessel extraction, marching-cubes surface models, and CUDA ray-casting volume rendering — entirely through a browser with server-side compute and zero installation.
