Its key claim is architectural rather than algorithmic: classical segmentation and hardware-accelerated visualization wrapped in a Redis/WebSocket server stack to enable ubiquitous, collaborative clinical access. Validation is limited to rendering throughput benchmarks and a single clinical case, with no segmentation accuracy evaluation and no learning-based components.

title: Automated segmentation of 3D anatomical structures on CT images by using a deep convolutional network based on end-to-end learning approach
architecture: 2D fully convolutional network (convolution 'coarse recognition' + deconvolution 'fine extraction') applied per 2D section, with 3D integration via majority voting across axial/sagittal/coronal orientations; preceded by a non-deep-learning organ localization module (Haar-like/LBP sliding window + group-wise Hough voting calibration) that restricts input to organ bounding boxes
main_contribution: The paper adds a non-deep-learning organ localization module (bounding-box detection) in front of the authors' previously published 2D fully convolutional network with 3D majority voting, restricting CNN training and testing to organ ROIs. On 12 test CT scans, this ROI restriction raised mean 3D Jaccard from 31% to 65% for pancreas and 80% to 88% for left kidney over their prior whole-image approach. The key finding — that cheap classical localization substantially boosts deep segmentation of difficult organs — is sound but preliminary, with a tiny test set, no statistical analysis, and no external benchmarks.

title: Segmentation of inner and outer bladder wall using deep-learning convolutional neural networks in CT urography
main_contribution: Extends the authors' prior outer-bladder-wall DL-CNN (Cha et al. 2016) to segment both inner and outer bladder wall in CT urography by generating a per-pixel wall likelihood map with a 5-layer Krizhevsky-style CNN and refining contours via level sets. Achieves 87.6%/87.2% test volume intersection (inner/outer wall) on 15 held-out cases, handling contrast/non-contrast wall appearance variation and prostate overlap imperfectly. Contribution is incremental within an in-house CAD pipeline: 2D patch classification (not volumetric segmentation), single institution, no Dice, no quantitative baseline comparison.

title: Towards dense volumetric pancreas segmentation in CT using 3D fully convolutional networks
main_contribution: The paper presents a custom multi-GPU 3D U-Net using same-size (zero-padded) convolutions to densely segment the whole pancreas in a single pass, eliminating the discontinuity artifacts of tiled subvolume inference. It systematically compares concatenation versus summation skip connections, showing that residual-style summation (12M vs 25M parameters) improves test Dice. Achieving 89.7 +/- 3.8% Dice on 147 gastric-cancer CT scans, it reported the state of the art for pancreas segmentation at the time, with <10-second inference per case.

A tutorial-style demonstration that a custom 3D U-Net trained end-to-end with a differentiable multi-class Dice loss achieves state-of-the-art ~89% mean Dice across 7 abdominal structures (liver, spleen, stomach, pancreas, gallbladder, artery, portal vein) on 377 contrast-enhanced gastric-cancer CTs. It shows such 3D FCNs are trainable on a single 24GB GPU using small random subvolumes, batch norm, and aggressive B-spline/rotation/translation augmentation, with sub-minute inference. Key limitations acknowledged: no anatomical/shape constraints, allowing disconnected or isolated segmentation regions.

title: Automatic Liver Segmentation in CT Volumes with Improved 3D U-net
main_contribution: The paper presents an engineering-focused improvement of the 3D U-Net for single-organ (liver) CT segmentation, combining dilated convolution stacks (rates 1-6), depth-wise separable convolutions, denser encoder skip concatenations, and SeLU activation, plus a simple HU-threshold-based post-processing step that removes false positives below 0 HU. On a single-center private dataset it reports DSC 0.961 +/- 0.013, numerically above two prior deep-learning methods, though on non-comparable test data and without ablation isolating each component's contribution. The main value for the review is as an example of efficient 3D architecture modifications (separable/dilated convolutions reduce computation for volumetric processing) and HU-prior post-processing; its evidence quality is low due to undisclosed patient counts, annotation protocol, and loss function, with no external validation or code release.

title: 3D Anisotropic Convolutional Neural Network with Step Transfer Learning for Liver Segmentation
architecture: Encoder-decoder CNN with ResNet encoder, atrous convolutions and ASPP; 3D anisotropic ensemble of three 2D segmentation networks (axial, coronal, sagittal)
main_contribution: Proposes a 2.5D '3D anisotropic' ensemble of three DeepLabV3-style encoder-decoder networks (ResNet backbones with atrous convolutions and ASPP) that segment liver from axial, coronal, and sagittal slice triplets, fused by averaging to exploit between-slice context without full 3D memory cost. Introduces Step Transfer Learning, a staged fine-tuning schedule that first trains randomly initialized layers while freezing ImageNet-pretrained encoder weights, improving over standard transfer learning. Achieves Dice 0.9485 / mIoU 0.9508 on LiTS liver segmentation, with ablations showing each component (anisotropic fusion, STL, deeper ResNet) contributes gains.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks Based Level Set Framework for Pancreas Segmentation from CT Images
architecture: Hybrid U-Net + Distance Regularized Level Set Evolution (DRLSE)
main_contribution: Proposes a three-stage pipeline for pancreas CT segmentation: fractional differential enhancement to boost pancreas-to-tissue contrast, a standard 2D U-Net producing a coarse initial region converted to a signed-distance initial contour, and distance regularized level set evolution (DRLSE) for boundary refinement. On 20 ISICDM2018 CT scans (evaluated on 20 2D slices), it reports mean Dice 0.82 and VD 0.15, beating four classical active contour baselines (CV, GAC, LBF, IVC). Its value is a simple demonstration that CNN initialization makes level set evolution viable for pancreas segmentation under very limited data, though the evaluation is too small and baselines too weak to establish clinical or SOTA relevance.

title: Deep Interactive Segmentation of Uncertain Regions with Shadowed Sets
main_contribution: Proposes a semi-automatic pancreas segmentation framework combining a 3D U-Net initial segmentation with shadowed sets theory (Pedrycz) to explicitly demarcate uncertain boundary regions, which are then targeted for focused two-round expert correction. On a private 20-scan Changhai Hospital CT dataset, this raises mean Dice from 0.65 (3D U-Net baseline) to 0.78. Key novelty is the three-way (confident/uncertain) shadowed-set partitioning of the probability map to reduce interaction scope, rather than a new deep architecture.

title: Segmenting Thoracic Cavities with Neoplastic Lesions: A Head-to-head Benchmark with Fully Convolutional Neural Networks
architecture: Benchmark of four fully convolutional architectures: 3D U-Net, V-Net (modified), 2D U-Net, two-stage 3D U-Net (best performer)
main_contribution: This paper presents the first head-to-head benchmark of four fully convolutional architectures (3D U-Net, modified V-Net, 2D U-Net, and two-stage 3D U-Net) under identical pre/post-processing pipelines and loss for segmenting lungs containing neoplastic disease, using the 402-scan expert-curated PleThora dataset — the largest public resource of its kind. All models achieved high performance (best Dice 0.947/0.952 left/right with the two-stage 3D U-Net; 3D U-Net best on ASSD bilaterally), with 3D models consistently superior to 2D on surface-distance metrics, though all remained below human inter-observer agreement. Clinical stratification identified systematic failure subgroups — stage I disease, female patients (suggesting potential sex bias), and rare anatomic outliers such as collapsed lungs — and showed that preprocessing choice materially shifts absolute performance, guiding both future data curation and fair benchmarking practice.

Demonstrates population-scale clinical deployment of a deep learning liver segmentation tool (3D U-Net trained on MSD with CycleGAN contrast-to-noncontrast domain transfer) for fully automated hepatic fat quantification on noncontrast CT in 9,552 adults, achieving close agreement with manual ROI measurement (mean difference 2.7 HU, r²≈0.92) and a 0.06% algorithm failure rate. Reports >50% prevalence of at least mild steatosis in an asymptomatic screening cohort and quantifies 5.5-year longitudinal steatosis shifts. For this segmentation review its value is evidence of real-world robustness and domain-adaptation practice, not architectural novelty; segmentation performance metrics are deferred to the companion technical paper.

title: Fully Automatic Volume Measurement of the Spleen at CT Using Deep Learning
main_contribution: A patch-based 3D U-Net segments the spleen on thoraco-abdominal oncology CT with Dice 0.962, statistically indistinguishable from a human observer (P=.834), using a two-stage model-assisted annotation strategy in which a first model (Dice 0.950) triages 1000 unlabeled scans so only 300 need manual correction. Beyond segmentation accuracy, an observer study (n=100) shows radiologist accuracy for splenic volume-change classification rises from 81% (visual) to 92% when algorithm-assisted, demonstrating clinical utility. Main weaknesses are single-center data and unreported training details (loss, optimizer, framework).

title: Deep learning-based volumetry of the future liver remnants and prediction of candidates for major hepatectomy
architecture: 3D U-Net (ensemble of five 3D U-Net models, DL-FLRVS)
main_contribution: Develops DL-FLRVS, a five-model 3D U-Net pipeline segmenting whole liver, 8 Couinaud segments, hepatic/portal veins, and lesions on contrast-enhanced CT, with rule-based FLR volumetry and automatic candidate categorization for major hepatectomy. Its key novelty is a full clinical-workflow validation against both the current semi-automated standard (hepatic VCAR) and manual volumetry in real preoperative candidates and diverse pathologies — near-perfect volumetric agreement with humans (Spearman r=0.99), superior discrimination (AUC 0.89 vs 0.86, DeLong p<0.0001), yet identical binary surgical decisions in almost all cases. Unlike prior DL FLR work focused on technical feasibility or living-donor transplant, this targets hepatectomy planning specifically, with explicitly spectrum-broadened external validation.

title: A 2D–3D hybrid convolutional neural network for lung lobe auto-segmentation on standard slice thickness computed tomography of patients receiving radiotherapy
architecture: 2D–3D hybrid CNN (3D V-Net branch + dense-connected 2D CNN with hybrid feature fusion module)
organs: ["left upper lobe", "left lower lobe", "right upper lobe", "right middle lobe", "right lower lobe"]
main_contribution: This paper proposes a 2D–3D hybrid CNN (a V-Net 3D branch for volumetric context fused with a dense-connected 2D branch for intra-slice edge/texture detail) targeted at the clinically realistic but understudied problem of lung lobe segmentation on 5 mm slice-thickness radiotherapy planning CT of locally advanced NSCLC patients. On a 105-patient single-center cohort it achieves per-lobe DSC of 0.90–0.96, comparable to state-of-the-art results obtained on much thinner-slice data, and demonstrates clinical usability with 93.7% of contours accepted without correction. The main contribution is the anisotropic-data-aware hybrid architecture and the clinical-thickness validation, not a methodological advance validated beyond one center.

First study to fine-tune a commercial DLAS product (RT-Mind-AI/DpnUNet) for rectal cancer radiotherapy, showing that institution-specific fine-tuning with only 60 real-world patients significantly improves CTV delineation (DSC +9–11%, eliminating vendor-model over-contouring) and small intestine segmentation while leaving bladder and femoral head performance (already adequate) essentially unchanged. It also provides a clinically relevant generalizability test demonstrating no performance degradation after a CT scanner change (Siemens → Philips), supporting the robustness of locally fine-tuned commercial DLAS in evolving clinical environments.

title: Automated and robust organ segmentation for 3D-based internal dose calculation
main_contribution: Extends Mask R-CNN to a lightweight 2.5D configuration (ResNet50-FPN, 28x28 RoI pooling, 256x256 masks) for automated kidney and liver CT segmentation with near-zero preprocessing, achieving Dice 93.4 (liver, LiTS) and up to 94.6 (kidney, external multi-centre validation) at clinically routine speed on consumer hardware. Its distinctive contribution is closing the loop to clinical outcome: automated 177Lu-DOTATOC kidney dosimetry differed from expert calculations by only 7.5% (mass) and 6.7% (self-absorbed dose), while demonstrating that automation still requires expert oversight due to SPECT-CT misregistration and fixed spill-out margins.

title: Automation of Wilms' tumor segmentation by artificial intelligence
main_contribution: The paper shows that a standard U-Net fails at fully automatic segmentation of Wilms' tumor and neoplastic kidney in pediatric CT on a very small single-center dataset (Dice 0.69/0.27), and proposes instead a semi-automatic training scheme (OV2ASSION) where experts annotate only sparse slices. With expert input at expert-equivalent gaps (1 in ~5 slices manual), Dice reaches inter-expert level (0.95 tumor / 0.91 kidney) while cutting expert time by ~80%. The main value for the field is a negative result plus a realistic human-in-the-loop fallback and an explicit call for a shared international pediatric Wilms' tumor CT database (KiTS19-style), rather than a deployable automatic method.

Proof-of-concept of SimpleDose, a fully automated whole-body [177Lu]Lu-PSMA dosimetry pipeline for 360° CZT SPECT/CT that combines nnU-Net-based 23-structure segmentation (public-data-trained model plus an HU-threshold bone marrow/cortical bone split) with collapsed-cone superposition to compute patient-specific voxel-level dose rates. In 10 patients it matched the MIRDcalc reference within ~5% median deviation for most soft-tissue organs in ~161 s, and demonstrated 14-min multi-time-point and ~3.5-min single-time-point dosimetry. For this segmentation-focused review, the paper evidences off-the-shelf deep-learning segmentation deployed reliably enough for clinical dosimetry, but contributes no segmentation accuracy evaluation of its own.

title: Generalizable deep learning framework for 3D medical image segmentation using limited training data
organs: ["skeletal bone structures", "orbita (orbital floor bone)", "eyes", "mandible", "cranium", "cardiac blood pool (heart chambers and connected vessels)", "bone (cardiac task)", "fetus", "lung parenchyma", "lung vessels", "trachea"]
main_contribution: The paper introduces a generalizable, resource-light clinical segmentation framework: a single fixed-hyperparameter 2D U-Net applied tri-planarly with probability-averaging consensus fusion and standardized augmentation/post-processing, integrated into the commercial Segment 3DPrint software, achieving average Dice 0.92±0.06 across six 3D-printing tasks using only 3-40 training subjects per task and ~10 s inference on a consumer GPU. A training-set-size ablation (Dice plateau from n=3) and a zero-shot knee experiment (Dice 0.95) support the central claim that local texture/intensity learning suffices for data-efficient, anatomy-agnostic segmentation of bone and high-contrast structures. For systematic review purposes, the contribution is strongest as clinical-translation and data-efficiency evidence, but is weakened by the absence of SOTA comparisons (e.g., nnU-Net), lack of external test validation, proprietary code, and untested soft-tissue organs.

title: Multi-scale U-like network with attention mechanism for automatic pancreas segmentation
architecture: 2.5D U-Net with hybrid attention (multi-scale U-like network)
main_contribution: The paper proposes a 2.5D U-shaped network that mixes 3D convolutions (first two encoder layers) with 2D convolutions, dense convolution blocks, and a hybrid spatial+channel attention module in the skip connections, embedded in a Zhou-style cascaded coarse-to-fine, three-view framework with majority-vote fusion. It achieves 86.61±3.47 mean DSC (max 92.03, min 73.89) on the NIH pancreas benchmark with 4-fold CV, outperforming prior methods with modest compute (7.3M parameters, trainable on a GTX 1060) and improved stability (higher minimum DSC, fewer low-DSC slices). The contribution is an accuracy/compute trade-off for small-organ segmentation, but the evidence base is a single small public dataset, Dice-only evaluation, no statistical testing, and no code release.

title: Liver tumor segmentation method combining multi-axis attention and conditional generative adversarial networks
architecture: MA-cGAN: U-Net-based 3D generator with multi-axis attention + 3-layer convolutional conditional GAN discriminator
main_contribution: Proposes MA-cGAN, a conditional GAN whose generator is a 3D U-Net augmented with multi-axis attention that projects volumes onto all three anatomical planes and fuses them via learnable weights, paired with a conditional convolutional discriminator and a Tversky + Wasserstein loss to handle tumor class imbalance and GAN instability. Achieves Dice 96.95 (liver) / 78.53 (tumor) with HD95 2.15 / 12.12 on a LiTS subset, outperforming seven CNN/Transformer baselines at only 4.99M parameters. Key caveats: single-dataset internal validation, no statistical significance testing, and slower convergence than purely supervised models.

title: MHub.ai: A Standardized Platform for Reproducible AI Research in Medical Imaging
architecture: Not a single architecture; platform packaging 30 pretrained models (incl. nnU-Net-based TotalSegmentator, LungMask, pulmonary lobe relational model, MONAI Model Zoo model)
main_contribution: MHub.ai is an open-source, container-based platform that standardizes inference-time distribution of 30 peer-reviewed medical imaging AI models via a unified DICOM-native application interface, structured metadata, and built-in reproducibility tests (sample input/reference output with Dice<0.99 deviation gating), raising deployment standardization from 36% to 99% on the authors' rubric. Its utility is demonstrated by benchmarking three lung segmentation models (TotalSegmentator v1, LungMask, LungLobes) on 422 NSCLC-Radiomics chest CTs using identical one-line docker commands, with per-organ Dice, paired t-tests, age correlations, and full case-level public dashboards. The key contribution to 3D organ segmentation research is not a new model but reproducible benchmarking infrastructure that removes setup friction and enables side-by-side comparison of existing organ segmentation models on clinical DICOM data.

title: Automatic Segmentation of Clinical Target Volume and Organs-at-Risk for Breast Conservative Radiotherapy Using a Convolutional Neural Network
main_contribution: This paper proposes U-ResNet, a 2.5D U-Net variant whose encoder is fully replaced by ResNet34, with a self-adaptive weighted cross-entropy loss enabling one-pass joint segmentation of breast CTV and five OARs for breast-conserving radiotherapy planning. On 160 single-center patients it modestly but significantly outperforms a same-configuration U-Net (CTV DSC 0.94 vs 0.93, P=0.001), achieves CTV 95HD (4.31 mm) better than prior deep-learning reports, and is the first study to clinically validate combined CTV+OAR auto-contouring for this setting — blinded oncologist scoring showed AI contours equivalent to ground truth (10 s vs 20–30 min). Its main value to the review is clinical-translation evidence (blinded expert evaluation, time savings) rather than architectural novelty, with generalizability limited by the single-center, non-3D design and no code release.

This study applies a previously developed fully-automated 3D U-Net hepatosplenic segmentation tool to categorize hepatic steatosis on contrast-enhanced CT in 1204 healthy adults, using unenhanced-CT-derived PDFF as the reference standard. It demonstrates that categorical steatosis assessment is feasible on contrast-enhanced CT (AUC up to 0.962-0.986 for moderate steatosis, e.g., <90 HU threshold: 75.9% sensitivity/95.7% specificity), performs substantially worse for mild (5%) steatosis, and finds no added value from splenic attenuation. For this review, it counts as evidence that deep-learning liver/spleen segmentation runs fully autonomously at scale (100% success on 1204 scans) to enable opportunistic NAFLD screening, though it provides no segmentation accuracy metrics itself.

title: Kidney and Kidney Tumor Segmentation using a Logical Ensemble of U-nets with Volumetric Validation
main_contribution: A challenge-entry method fusing three standard 2D U-Nets (lax kidney+tumor, strict kidney+tumor, tumor-only) via logical bitwise AND, followed by a rule-based 3D volumetric validation step (volume, position, morphology, sphericity, and cross-frame consistency thresholds) applied to stacked 2D predictions. The main contribution is demonstrating that cheap anatomically-informed post-hoc 3D filtering of 2D outputs improves per-class F1 (kidney 0.80->0.85, tumor 0.45->0.50) without the cost of a 3D network. Performance remains below clinical utility — tumor precision is poor (0.40) from over-segmentation — and no external or SOTA comparison is provided.

title: RA-UNet: A Hybrid Deep Attention-Aware Network to Extract Liver and Tumor in CT Scans
architecture: RA-UNet (residual attention-aware U-Net), two-stage cascade: RA-UNet-I (2D, coarse liver localization) + RA-UNet-II (3D, liver and tumor segmentation)
main_contribution: RA-UNet couples a 2D coarse liver-localization stage (RA-UNet-I) with a 3D residual attention-aware U-Net (RA-UNet-II) that sequentially segments liver then tumor in a cascade, claiming the first application of attention residual learning to 3D medical volume segmentation via a compact ~4M-parameter from-scratch model. It reaches 0.961 per-case liver / 0.595 tumor Dice on the LiTS test set and transfers to 3DIRCADb at 0.977 / 0.830, outperforming listed 2D baselines on liver and beating Christ et al.'s CFCN (0.56) on 3DIRCADb tumors. The advance is architectural (attention residual modules inside a 3D U-Net plus voting ensembling) rather than a new training paradigm; tumor segmentation — not organ segmentation — remains the weak point.

title: Three-Dimensional Liver Image Segmentation Using Generative Adversarial Networks Based on Feature Restoration
architecture: Semi-supervised DCGAN with improved 3D U-Net as discriminator and feature-restoration DCNN as generator
main_contribution: The paper proposes a semi-supervised 3D DCGAN framework for liver CT segmentation in which the discriminator is an improved 3D U-Net (SE channel attention + pyramid pooling) and the generator produces realistic fake 3D volumes by restoring them from real feature maps instead of random noise, addressing labeled-data scarcity in 3D medical segmentation. It achieves Dice 0.9424 on LiTS-2017 test and 0.959 on KiTS19, outperforming baseline 3D U-Net and several published methods, while candidly reporting efficiency limitations (~150M parameters, ~50 h training on one GPU).

title: Mamba-enhanced codebook learning with anatomical constraints for liver and tumor segmentation in 3D CT volumes
architecture: Hierarchical 3D U-Net with Mamba-based global relational module and vector-quantization codebook module
main_contribution: Proposes a hierarchical 3D U-Net for liver and tumor segmentation in CT that couples a multi-scale context encoder with a Mamba-based module at the bottleneck for linear-complexity cross-slice dependency modeling, plus a vector-quantization codebook (K=64) that enforces compact, discriminative feature representations. An inclusion loss embeds the anatomical prior that tumors must reside within the liver, regularizing outputs and reducing false positives. On an internal re-split of LiTS, the method outperforms eight baselines with liver Dice 0.94 / tumor Dice 0.47 at ~0.04 s per sample, with ablations confirming each module's individual contribution.

title: Automatic renal mass segmentation and classification on CT images based on 3D U-Net and ResNet algorithms
main_contribution: This paper presents a fully automated cascaded pipeline for renal mass characterization: a 3D U-Net segments bilateral kidneys as ROI, an ensemble 3D U-Net segments masses on the cropped volume, and a 10-layer 3D ResNet classifies masses as AML, cystic, or solid, with Grad-CAM for interpretability. Trained on 610 contrast-enhanced CT series (490 patients), it achieves near-perfect kidney DSC (0.99 test) and moderate mass DSC (0.75/0.83 test, degrading to 0.68/0.64 on KiTS21 and ~0.70–0.72 externally), with 90.56% classification accuracy (91.97% for ≥5 mm masses). The main contributions are the two-stage ROI-cropping design (shown superior to a one-stage ablation) and demonstration of cross-dataset generalization, though clinical utility is bounded by moderate mass-segmentation accuracy, detection precision near 60–68%, and absent pathology-based confirmation.

This paper demonstrates a fully automatic 2D U-Net (implemented in the non-standard commercial LabVIEW/DeepLTK stack) trained on 135 multi-center patients with normal, ARDS, and COVID-19 lungs, segmenting a complete CT scan in ~5 seconds versus 1–2 hours of manual work, with test IoU of 87.3% overall and clinically acceptable agreement on downstream CT-qa variables (lung volume bias −9.8 ml, R²=0.99; recruitability bias ≤0.5%). Its key strengths for the review are validation at the level of clinically actionable variables (recruitability, tissue fractions) rather than mask overlap alone, and unusually transparent failure analysis (apex/base errors, pleural effusion confusion, overfitting signs). It is limited by a 2D slice-wise (non-3D) approach, MSE loss, absence of external validation, no Dice or boundary metrics, and zero code/data availability due to proprietary tooling.

title: Deep-learning-based automatic liver segmentation using computed tomography images in dogs
main_contribution: This is the first deep learning model for automated liver segmentation in canine abdominal CT, addressing an unmet need in veterinary medicine. Using a 3D U-Net trained on 221 single-institution CT scans, the authors achieved mean DSC of 0.926–0.929 and volume correlations of r ≥ 0.995, matching top human LiTS benchmark performance despite inter-breed anatomical variability and modest data. The two-experiment design (normal livers vs. combined with/without hepatic masses) establishes a baseline for interpreting performance degradation on morphologically complex, mass-containing livers and demonstrates feasibility of clinical veterinary liver volumetry for diagnosing hepatomegaly/microhepatica and monitoring postoperative regeneration.

title: Boundary Loss-Based 2.5D Fully Convolutional Neural Networks Approach for Segmentation: A Case Study of the Liver and Tumor on Computed Tomography
architecture: Cascaded 2.5D Fully Convolutional Neural Networks (FCNs) with residual blocks
main_contribution: The paper proposes a cascaded 2.5D residual FCN framework with a novel boundary loss (distance + area + boundary terms, applied after initial combined CE+Dice optimization) and structure-specific post-processing (3D connected components for liver; dense CRF + HU-based FP/FN filtering for tumor) for liver and tumor segmentation in contrast-enhanced CT. It reports LiTS Dice Per Case of 94.3% (liver) and 74.5% (tumor) using only ~4 GB VRAM (~6x less than H-DenseUNet), positioning boundary-aware supervision as an effective, memory-efficient alternative to fully 3D networks, though liver Dice still trails the best 3D baselines. Reproducibility and generalizability are limited by the absence of released code, incomplete training details, no true external validation, and comparisons restricted to older baseline methods.

This multicenter technical note retrospectively evaluates a commercial 3D U-Net auto-contouring system (ART-Plan/TheraPanacea) as a 'predictive peer review' tool across three Italian radiotherapy centers, comparing manual, AI, and AI-adjusted contours in 62 hypofractionated prostate cancer patients. It reports that AI-adjusted contours agree significantly more with the AI reference than manual contours do (CTV median DSC 0.80→0.92; HDmax 12.33→9.52 mm; all p<0.0001, large effect sizes), supporting reduced interobserver variability and workflow standardization via a physician-as-reviewer paradigm. Its contribution is a clinical workflow/validation paradigm rather than a novel segmentation algorithm, with the central methodological weakness of using the AI output itself as the ground truth reference.

title: Point-Sampling Method Based on 3D U-Net Architecture to Reduce the Influence of False Positive and Solve Boundary Blur Problem in 3D CT Image Segmentation
main_contribution: Render 3D U-Net reframes 3D CT organ segmentation as a rendering problem, replacing standard decoder upsampling with a PointRend-inspired subdivision-based point-sampling scheme inside a 3D attention-gated nested U-Net (3D ANU-Net) trained under deep supervision with a hybrid Dice + Hausdorff-distance boundary loss, and adds a False Positive Classification (FPC) module that zeroes out predictions when organ presence is not detected. On internal 5:1 splits of LiTS (liver), KiTS (kidney), and segTHOR (heart) as single-organ binary tasks, it reported Dice of 96.08/95.89/96.12 with reduced Hausdorff distance versus seven U-Net-family baselines, with ablations attributing gains to point-sampling and FPC. The methodological novelty (boundary-focused rendering and explicit false-positive suppression) is notable, but evaluation rigor is limited by missing reproducibility details, no external validation, and no statistical analysis.

Applies a 2D ResU-Net (U-Net with pre-activated residual blocks) plus a standard pre-processing pipeline (HU windowing, histogram equalization, flip/rotation augmentation, weighted cross-entropy) to liver and liver-tumor segmentation on 3D-IRCADb01, reporting DSC 0.978 (liver) and 0.893 (tumor). The contribution is incremental — an established architecture with conventional pre-processing and no novel methodological component. Evidence strength is limited by 20 subjects, an undefined train/test split, no external validation, and internal inconsistencies between abstract and reported tables.

title: G-UNETR++: A Gradient-Enhanced Network for Accurate and Robust Liver Segmentation from Computed Tomography Images
main_contribution: G-UNETR++ extends UNETR++ with two parallel gradient-based encoders consuming second-order partial derivatives (∂²f/∂x∂z, ∂²f/∂y∂z from the CT Hessian matrix) to explicitly learn 3D organ-boundary geometry, paired with a Dice+CE+Hausdorff hybrid loss. It reports liver Dice of 97.38% (LiTS), 97.50% (3D-IRCADb), and 97.32% (Sliver07), outperforming 18 compared methods, but at 97.73M parameters (~2.3× the UNETR++ baseline) — 'moderate' only relative to nnFormer. The contribution is single-organ (liver) with external validation on two independent public datasets; no code is released, which limits verification and reuse.

The paper proposes an online hard-example enhancement strategy for CT organ segmentation: a pre-training model trained on one half of the training set acts as a task-specific hard/easy slice classifier (thresholded at the baseline's worst-case Dice), and flip-augmented hard slices are then added back to the training data to rebalance dataset-level hard/easy sample imbalance — something the authors argue Dice loss or focal loss alone cannot fix. Across FCN and U-Net on liver, kidney, and spleen segmentation, the method yields small mean Dice gains (~0.8-1.5 points) with consistent improvement on worst-case (min) Dice. A secondary empirical finding is substantial slice redundancy in CT training sets: reducing training volumes to 50% barely affects performance, while reductions below 30% degrade it sharply.

This paper proposes SECP-Net, a 2D cascaded U-shape network for CT organs-at-risk segmentation in nasopharyngeal carcinoma that introduces (1) SE-Connection (SEC) modules — channel-attention-gated cross-level feature fusion replacing naive U-Net skip connections — and (2) a stage-wise pyramid structure for multi-scale and global context propagation, combined with auto-context cascading of a secondary U-Net for refinement. On a 356-patient private NPC cohort it achieves the best mean Dice (83.28%) versus seven baselines, with the largest gains on small organs (eyes, submandibular glands, thyroid), and confirms generalizability on the public LiTS liver/tumor benchmark. The main value for the review lies in its evidence that attention-based multi-scale feature fusion plus cascading improves small-OAR segmentation, though its explicitly 2D design, single-center private data, and re-implemented baselines under constrained hardware limit stronger conclusions.

Proposes SED, a two-stage series of encoder-decoder networks — U-Net for liver localization followed by FC-DenseNet for tumor segmentation within the masked liver region — motivated by reducing per-network task difficulty versus a single end-to-end model. On a mixed dataset of 4300 CT slices (LiTS + 400 institutional KCGMH images), it reports Dice scores of 0.92 (liver) and 0.75 (tumor), with 3D reconstruction of predicted lesions to support HCC surgical planning. Main limitations for review purposes: slice-level random split (possible patient leakage), single Dice metric, no external validation, and no code release.

Proposes a three-stage liver cancer CAD pipeline: a modified GAN for synthetic CT slice generation, a YOLOv3 detector with ResNet-50 backbone (dual-scale detection heads) for liver/tumor localization (0.99 mAP), and DeepLabv3 with an InceptionResNetV2 backbone for tumor segmentation (>95% accuracy). The main novelty claim is synthetic data augmentation to address small-lesion segmentation with limited training data. Note: the paper was retracted in 2026 and its '3D' segmentation claim is not supported by the 2D slice-based architecture.

title: Deep Segmentation Networks for Segmenting Kidneys and Detecting Kidney Stones in Unenhanced Abdominal CT Images
architecture: Two-stage coarse-to-fine training scheme with replaceable segmentation networks: 3D U-Net, Res U-Net, SegNet, DeepLabV3+, UNETR (best: Res U-Net)
main_contribution: This study contributes (1) the first open-access, radiologist-approved annotated dataset of 260 unenhanced abdominal CT scans with kidney and kidney-stone masks (Zenodo), addressing data scarcity for renal stone AI research, and (2) a two-stage coarse-to-fine training scheme with interchangeable backbones (3D U-Net, Res U-Net, SegNet, DeepLabV3+, UNETR) that improves segmentation over independent one-step training, achieving 96.54% kidney Dice and 80.59% stone Dice with Res U-Net. It further provides a systematic architecture benchmark and stone-size-stratified error analysis showing small stones (<6mm) remain the principal failure mode (Dice 60.11%).

title: Novel Domain Knowledge-Encoding Algorithm Enables Label-Efficient Deep Learning for Cardiac CT Segmentation to Guide Atrial Fibrillation Treatment in a Pilot Dataset
organs: ["left atrium body", "left superior pulmonary vein", "left inferior pulmonary vein", "right superior pulmonary vein", "right inferior pulmonary vein", "left atrial appendage"]
main_contribution: The paper introduces DOKEN, a domain-knowledge-encoding algorithm that automatically labels six left atrial substructures by morphological erosion-dilation parsing of cardiac geometry (tuned via SVMs on only 5 seed cases), enabling nnU-Net training on just 20 patients while validating on 100 hold-out cases — an inverted ~1:5 train:test ratio. It achieves Dice 96.7%, 1.51 mm median surface distance, and expert-level correlation (r=0.99), parsing 28/34 anatomical variants. The contribution is label-efficiency rather than accuracy superiority over SOTA: it lacks external validation, per-structure results, head-to-head baselines, and released code.

This paper provides the first intermodal (CT vs CMR) clinical validation of a commercial deep learning model for fully automated quantification of all four cardiac chamber volumes and LV myocardial mass on routine non-contrast chest CT, addressing the gap left by prior intramodal-only validation. In 53 paired patients, ventricular volumes and LV mass correlated well-to-excellently with CMR (ICC 0.78-0.91) with ~98% processing success and no significant dependence on ECG-gating, while atrial volumes performed only moderately (ICC 0.61-0.74) with systematic overestimation. The work supports using opportunistic non-gated chest CT as a screening adjunct for incidentally detecting cardiac dilation/hypertrophy, though the proprietary, non-reproducible model limits scientific transparency.

A head-to-head clinical validation of two RVX Liver Segmentation workflows and TotalSegmentator against manual segmentation on 86 healthy-adult CTs, showing clinically acceptable volumetric agreement (Dice 0.911–0.946) with 4–60× time reductions (0.64–10.42 min vs 40.42 min manual). TotalSegmentator offered the best speed/accuracy trade-off with no significant volume bias (+14.4 cm³), while the RVX deep-learning mode was fastest but systematically overestimated volume (+45.8 cm³ bias, highest HD, 9.3% over-segmentation rate). This is an application/evaluation study of pretrained tools, not a model-development paper — the rubric's architecture, training, and split criteria are largely inapplicable.

title: Numerical Evaluation on Parametric Choices Influencing Segmentation Results in Radiology Images—A Multi-Dataset Study
main_contribution: An empirical ablation study evaluating how weight initialization, activation function, loss function, and optimizer choices affect CNN segmentation performance, using 3D U-Net on MSD (liver, pancreas, cardiac) and VGG-16 on LiTS liver data, scored with eight metrics plus paired t-tests. Best combinations identified: Glorot+Adam+CE for 3D U-Net (liver Dice 0.897, pancreas 0.691) and Glorot+tanh+CE for VGG-16 (liver Dice 0.921). The contribution is practical guidance on hyperparameter selection rather than a new architecture; notably, Dice-loss configurations failed outright on pancreas, differences between configurations were small, and no external state-of-the-art comparison was performed.

This paper proposes FG-CKD-UNet, a dual-headed multitask U-Net that jointly performs multi-compartment kidney segmentation (cortex/medulla/pelvis) and eGFR prediction, coupled through a novel structure-function consistency loss and an embedded differentiable morphological biomarker extractor (cortical thickness, compartment volumes, cortex-medulla ratio). On a 100-subject T2-weighted MRI CKD dataset it reports Dice 0.94 / HD95 9.8 mm and eGFR MAE 0.039 / Pearson r 0.92, with the consistency loss reducing consistency error from 0.071 to 0.042. For a review focused on 3D CT organ segmentation, its relevance is limited: the method is 2D slice-based, primarily MRI-driven, and its CT 'external validation' uses colorized 2D images without segmentation masks.

This paper proposes FF-ResUNet, a privacy-preserving split-learning segmentation framework in which each institution runs a residual U-Net encoder locally and transmits only a compact 16×16×512 bottleneck tensor to a central server, eliminating the high-resolution skip-connection features that dominate both privacy leakage risk and bandwidth cost in collaborative U-Nets. A purpose-built server-side decoder (multi-scale dilated convolutions, residual refinement, progressive bilinear upsampling, boundary-aware loss) compensates for the absent skip fusion, achieving LiTS liver/tumor Dice of 0.952/0.737 with the best tumor boundary error (HD95 10.9 mm) while cutting per-iteration communication by 92–98% (~480 MB → ~8 MB), at a quantified cost of ~1.6 tumor Dice points versus a full-skip equivalent. Cross-domain evaluation on 3D-IRCADb and AMOS-CT under simulated multi-institution partitions demonstrates robust generalization, positioning the work as a practical privacy–bandwidth–accuracy compromise for multi-center deployment rather than an accuracy-maximizing method.

title: Lung and Infection CT-Scan-Based Segmentation with 3D UNet Architecture and Its Modification
architecture: 3D UNet plus three modified variants: 3D ResUNet, 3D VGGUNet, 3D DenseUNet
main_contribution: This study benchmarks the original 3D UNet against three encoder-modified variants (3D ResUNet/ResNet152, 3D VGGUNet/VGG19, 3D DenseUNet/DenseNet201, each with and without ImageNet transfer learning, totaling 7 models per task) for lung (binary) and lung+infection (3-class) segmentation on COVID-19 CT volumes, using a combined Dice+focal loss and fully volumetric 128^3 processing to avoid 2D slicing. Surprisingly, vanilla 3D UNet achieved the best results (Dice 97.05% lung; 88.61% lung+infection; IoU 94.32%/81.58%), outperforming all modified backbones, and the authors highlight 3D infection projections for clinical severity grading as the practical benefit. The evidence base is weak, however: only 20 CT volumes (5 test), no external validation, no statistical testing, and no code release limit the reliability and reproducibility of the conclusions.

title: Segmentation of Pancreatic Subregions in Computed Tomography Images
architecture: Multistage anatomy-guided 3D U-Net with naïve Bayes soft-label integration
main_contribution: First automated 3D method for segmenting pancreatic subregions (head/body/tail) in contrast-enhanced CT, using a naïve Bayes model over anatomical priors (subregion length and volumetric proportions) to generate soft-label probability maps that are fused per-epoch with a 3D U-Net via joint-probability renormalization. The anatomy guidance yields ~8% mean DSC improvement over plain U-Net, reaching 94.5/95.6/89.9% on healthy (NIH), pre-cancerous (D1), and cancerous (D2) cohorts, with cross-dataset transfer demonstrating robustness to pancreatic pathology. Also contributes new expert subregional reference labels for the entire public NIH Pancreas-CT dataset.

The paper introduces AuraViT-FL, a resource-efficient 2D hybrid Vision Transformer–CNN segmentation framework (ViT encoder + ASPP + attention-gated U-Net decoder) trained with a FedProx-based federated learning pipeline featuring adaptive weighted aggregation and dynamic virtual client partitioning for privacy-preserving lung tumor segmentation, achieving 80.81% mean Dice with <1% degradation versus centralized training. It further proposes lightweight LAURA variants (down to ~5.5M parameters, >96% reduction) that retain competitive Dice (up to 82.96% on MSD Lung), with ablations showing smaller encoders can match or beat the full model. The evidence supports decentralized training feasibility, though slice-level evaluation, simulated federation, and non-comparable cross-study baselines temper the strength of the SOTA claims.

title: Deep Learning Model with Attention Mechanism for a 3D Pancreas Segmentation in CT Scans
architecture: 3D Attention U-Net (3D U-Net encoder-decoder with attention gates at skip connections)
main_contribution: This paper proposes a lightweight 3D Attention U-Net (channels 2→16) with attention gates at all skip connections, trained with a Dice+Focal loss for binary pancreas segmentation in contrast-enhanced CT, achieving 80.8±2.1% DSC (ASSD 2.1 mm, HD95 8.1 mm) on the NIH dataset and 78.1±1.1% DSC (ASSD 3.3 mm, HD95 12.3 mm) on MSD with fast inference (~2.7 s/case). Its key contributions are demonstrating that a computationally frugal attention-gated 3D architecture reaches competitive benchmark accuracy, and a statistically rigorous (Friedman + post-hoc) loss-function ablation showing Dice+Focal significantly outperforms Dice-only. Limitations include lack of code release, no external/cross-dataset validation, and non-comparable MSD label merging (pancreas+tumor).

This paper proposes a fully automated 2D U-Net variant for esophagus segmentation in chest CT that combines ImageNet-pretrained encoders (ResNet34/SEResNext50), a custom spatial attention module in the decoder, and group normalization, with a STAPLE-based fusion of k-fold cross-validation predictions as post-processing. Evaluated on both SegTHOR and StructSeg 2019, it achieves the best reported esophagus Dice (0.8690) and HD (0.2527) on the SegTHOR test set versus prior challenge methods, and demonstrates via cross-dataset experiments and ablations (attention type, backbone, GN vs BN) that the approach is effective and not overfit to a single dataset. The key insight is that lightweight 2D processing plus attention and probabilistic multi-fold label fusion can match or exceed 3D methods for a small, low-contrast organ while drastically reducing computational cost.

title: DG-TTA: Out-of-Domain Medical Image Segmentation Through Augmentation, Descriptor-Driven Domain Generalization, and Test-Time Adaptation
organs: ["spleen", "right kidney", "left kidney", "gallbladder", "esophagus", "liver", "stomach", "aorta", "inferior vena cava", "pancreas", "vertebral bodies L1-L5", "left ventricle", "right ventricle", "left atrium", "right atrium", "left ventricle myocardium", "ascending aorta", "pulmonary artery"]
main_contribution: DG-TTA combines domain-generalized nnUNet pre-training (GIN intensity augmentation plus SSC self-similarity context descriptor inputs) with a source-free, two-branch augmentation-consistency test-time adaptation (soft Dice loss, d=2) applied per unseen scan, integrated entirely within the standard 3D nnUNet pipeline. Across five public datasets and five CT-to-MR cross-domain scenarios (abdominal, lumbar spine, cardiac), it significantly improves over base nnUNet (up to +64.0% Dice on non-generalized models; p<0.001) and outperforms Tent, TTA-RMI, RSA, and AdaMI, reaching 78.6-82.6% mean Dice while closing most of the gap to in-domain training with minimal assumptions and released code.

title: Dual-Stage AI Model for Enhanced CT Imaging: Precision Segmentation of Kidney and Tumors
architecture: Dual-stage: SwinUNETR (ViT-based) for kidney segmentation + enhanced 3D UNet (Kidney Tumor 3D UNet) for tumor detection/segmentation
main_contribution: The paper proposes a dual-stage pipeline pairing a ViT-based SwinUNETR for kidney localization with a residual-block and attention-gate-enhanced 3D UNet for tumor segmentation, arguing that investment in stage-1 localization quality is critical to reduce false positives in stage 2. Its key empirical claim, supported by an ablation over SS/DS variants of nnUNet-3D and SwinUNETR on 1081 CECT scans with external validation, is that this design substantially raises small-tumor (<=4cm) detection sensitivity (0.90/0.89) while cutting false positives per patient (0.23/0.15) versus single-stage SOTA. Notably, training uses only public KiTS23 data, with a 592-scan private ccRCC cohort reserved entirely for external validation; main gaps are missing code, incompletely specified training schedules, and generalizability limited by the ccRCC-only external set.

title: Evaluation of a Deep Learning Algorithm for Automated Spleen Segmentation in Patients with Conditions Directly or Indirectly Affecting the Spleen
main_contribution: This is a controlled cross-dataset generalizability study showing that a 3D residual U-Net trained on normal spleens (MSD) fails on pathological abdomens (DSC 0.648 vs 0.941; RAVD 42% vs 4%), while a model trained on a pathology-enriched in-house cohort performs well on both distributions. The actionable finding for the field is that spleen segmentation models built on normal-anatomy datasets (including most MSD-trained models) cannot be assumed safe for clinical populations with splenomegaly, ascites, or perisplenic disease. The contribution is evidentiary rather than architectural - no new method is proposed.

title: Comparison of semi-automatic and deep learning-based automatic methods for liver segmentation in living liver transplant donors
main_contribution: This challenge-style study provides the first head-to-head comparison of deep learning automatic methods against six well-established semi-automatic methods for liver segmentation and volumetry in living liver transplant donors, demonstrating that DL methods now dominate (top 4 ranks all DL; best VO 90.4% METU_U-Net, best final score 79.6 ITU_U-Net) with higher accuracy and lower volume-estimation variability than interactive techniques. It further shows that ensemble fusion of DL outputs via STAPLE/MV raises performance to 86.0–88.7 at near-zero time cost when models run in parallel, and it contributes an expert-consensus-annotated donor CT dataset with a five-metric graded evaluation protocol and quantified intra-user ceiling (95.14).

title: Quality versus quantity of training datasets for artificial intelligence–based whole liver segmentation
main_contribution: First comprehensive controlled comparison of the annotation-quality vs. dataset-quantity tradeoff for AI-based whole-liver CT segmentation, training 3D nnU-Net models on 56-2,840 scans spanning highly curated and mixed-curation compositions. A 244-scan highly curated dataset matched a 2,840-scan mixed-curation dataset (10x larger) on 3D metrics (DSC 0.971, p>.999), while larger mixed-curation datasets improved generalizability on external BTCV data (Slice DSC 0.929 at 710 scans) and reduced worst-slice failures. The authors conclude the quality/quantity tradeoff is nuanced and goal-dependent: quality suffices when data are scarce and inference is in-distribution; quantity buys robustness out-of-distribution.
